In the first scenario, everything went as Ron said it did, only after he helped the guy back into his hotel room, the guy may not have ever woken up after falling asleep. If the investor did die, it's not likely that anyone would have reached out to tell Ron about it, especially if no one at the hotel witnessed the dropoff. The second scenario paints Ron as a darker character, in that it surmizes the accident was deadlier than Robinson's character let on, and he just dumped the body rather than reporting it to the proper authorities. Either way, nothing good for Ron's sanity, and definitely something that Lake Bell's Barb would continue worrying about for years and years to come. Theory #2: The Trip With The Investor Never Actually Happened This idea is related to the overarching theory that Ron is experiencing a complete mental collapse, where the majority of his experiences are believed to be mental constructs. However, it would make more sense, and possibly be more effective, if only some of Ron's daily motions were eventually revealed to be completely inside his own head. For instance: Ron's disturbed conversation with his dog made him seem self-aware that his Jeep Tours idea was lacking. So what if, instead of putting himself at risk of not getting any loans, Ron decided to just not meet up with any investors, and instead made up the entire trip. Then, instead of telling Barb he lied, or even that his ideas were turned down, what if Ron just made up the entire Jeep accident story on the spot and kept digging himself into a deeper hole? Imagine if Barb went outside to check on the Jeep and saw it was undamaged. It would be a disturbing sign of proof that her husband isn't everything she thinks. Lying about harming someone isn't that much better than legitimately harming the person. Now, that pair of theories wouldn't fully explain everything else that is or isn't happening in Ron's life, from the face model phone calls to the guy trying to buy Fab Four action figures to Douglas being rescued at home. But it'd definitely strengthen Barb and Natalie's innate worries about him, while possibly weakening his attempt to track down everyone involved with Tecca and the Red Ball. True to form for a unique comedic personality like Tim Robinson, The Chair Company is heading into its finale the same way it arrived: with viewers giggling, cringing and questioning what the hell is actually happening. Episode 7 capped off with a bonkers ending that inspired all kinds of predictions about the impending Season 1 finale. ( Season 2 has already been ordered up .) At no point during this first season did I suspect Lake Bell's Barb of being anything but exTREMEly patient and understanding with a man who makes every situation as uncomfortable as an iron maiden. Alice Quintana seemed to only get in touch with Barb for investing purposes after Ron found the photos and started digging more into Tecca. Search site Submit search Subscribe Newsletter Advertise News & City Arts & Entertainment Food & Drink Life & Style Events Sports Top Professionals Awards Travel Newsletter Sign Up Advertise News & City Arts & Entertainment Food & Drink Life & Style Events Sports Top Professionals Awards Travel Search Search site Submit search Baby2Baby Raises a Record $18 Million at Starriest Gala Yet Prince Harry, Meghan Markle, Lizzo, Nicole Richie, Orlando Bloom, Paris Hilton, Will Ferrell and others supported the event honoring Serena Williams Jasmin Rosemberg • November 9, 2025 Kelly Sawyer Patricof, Co-CEO, Baby2Baby, Serena Williams, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex and Norah Weinstein, Co-CEO, Baby2Baby Credit: Photo by Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for Baby2Baby Over the last 14 years, Baby2Baby has provided half a billion essential items (including diapers, formula and clothing) to children living in poverty across the country. However, this past year proved one of the most important in the organization’s history. “This year, Baby2Baby provided essentials to the one million children relying on them in foster care, homeless and domestic violence shelters, schools and more in all 50 states and 300 cities,” began presenter Olivia Munn from the stage of the Pacific Design Center on Saturday, Nov. 8 at the 2025 Baby2Baby Gala presented by Paul Mitchell. Jessica Alba, Kelly Sawyer Patricof, Co-CEO, Baby2Baby, Serena Williams, Norah Weinstein, Co-CEO, Baby2Baby and Olivia Munn Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby “I think that it might be hard for many of us in this room to comprehend the fact that 1 in 2 families in this country cannot afford diapers for their babies,” added Kerry Washington, who accompanied Munn to the podium. “And consider the ripple effect: If a mom doesn’t have enough diapers to drop her baby off at daycare, she can’t go to work. And so, the cycle of difficulty continues.” Olivia Munn and Kerry Washington Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Washington noted how Baby2Baby built its own diaper manufacturing system, making diapers for 80 percent less than retail cost and distributing over 250 million. “They’ve even successfully advocated to remove sales tax from diapers here in California,” she added, “and since then, 13 more states have followed suit.” Paris Hilton, Lizzo and Meghan Trainor Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Baby2Baby’s fastest-growing program is helping families in the wake of disasters. The organization’s work in this area began with Hurricane Harvey in 2017, when the team realized disaster relief areas did not have items to accommodate babies and children. Since then, Baby2Baby has responded to 100 disasters — from hurricanes in Florida to wildfires in Maui. But this year brought unforeseen challenges. Scroll to continue reading fresh drops This Week, the 9-2 LA Rams Travel Eastward to Duel the 6-6 Carolina Panthers World War II Hero, Artist and Activist Yoshio Nakamura Dies at 100 LA Grand Jury Hears Celeste Homicide Case as D4vd’s Santa Barbara Trip Is Confirmed In-N-Out Burger Owner Starts Homeless Non-Profit Paris Hilton, Demi Lovato, Nicole Richie, Kerry Washington and Katie Lowes Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby “Never in a million years did we think we would be up here this year, talking about our own backyards and city having been burned down — personally and profoundly impacting every single one of us in this room,” said Baby2Baby co-CEO Norah Weinstein. “On that horrific Tuesday morning in January when the fires broke out, our team immediately activated by reaching out to Baby2Baby’s 470 partners across Los Angeles,” added co-CEO Kelly Sawyer Patricof. “We deployed our fleet of trucks to deliver millions of diapers, in addition to food, water, hygiene products, clothing, underwear and socks, portable cribs, strollers and and air purifiers to children displaced by the fires.” Baby2Baby co-CEOs Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Baby2Baby also held drive-throughs at their headquarters in Culver City and hosted pop-up distributions across the city, from Pasadena to Dodger Stadium to Palisades Pre-School to provide essentials directly. The organization supplied gear to 100 additional fire relief events; sent diapers to the city, state and FEMA; and opened a storefront in Pasadena. “In total, so far, we have distributed 31 million emergency supplies to families,” Patricof said to applause. Read more about Weinstein and Patricof’s fire relief efforts in our March L.A. Woman issue . Orlando Bloom, Jessica Alba and Danny Ramirez Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Next up, they’re building a new national headquarters and warehouse in Santa Monica that will serve as Baby2Baby’s permanent home in 2027. This new 47,000-square-foot facility will triple its warehouse capacity and double its volunteer space, allowing it to help even more children. “This year, Baby2Baby served one million children around the country in all 50 states,” said Patricof. “We gave out our 500 millionth item, our 270 millionth diaper and our 10 millionth backpack and school supplies.” But they aspire to help the 10 million children still on their waitlist. Prior to sitting for the program, over 800 guests — including executives, business leaders, philanthropists and famous supporters, such as Adam Scott, Anna Kendrick, Ayesha Curry, Camila Alves McConaughey, Charlie Puth, Demi Lovato, Erin Foster, Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, Jenna Dewan, Judd Apatow, Julianne Hough, Kaley Cuoco, Katherine LaNasa, Lake Bell, Leslie Mann, Lizzo, Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, Meghan Trainor, Miranda Kerr, Missy Elliott, Molly Sims, Monique Lhuillier, Nicole Richie, Orlando Bloom, Paris Hilton, Rachel Zoe, Sara Foster, Swizz Beatz, Tyler Perry, Vanessa Bryant and Will Ferrell — mingled during a cocktail hour. They sipped Avaline wine and Casamigos, Johnnie Walker and Ketel One cocktails, and snacked on passed bites curated by Jon Shook & Vinny Dotolo. Then, the real eating began. Credit: Author A restaurant area offered dinner stations, featuring dishes by beloved eateries including Funke, Holy Basil, Kato, Kazunori by Sushi Nozawa, Burger She Wrote, The Benjamin Hollywood, Beethoven Market, 88 Club, A Ti, Max & Helen’s, Moo’s Craft Barbecue, Mr. Chow, Pizzeria Bianco and Saffy’s. Kazunori had the longest line (for custom toro, salmon, yellowtail, scallop and crab hand rolls), and other favorites included the matzoh ball soup from Phil Rosenthal’s new diner Max & Helen’s, the cacio e pepe from Funke, the honey sesame shrimp from Kato and the beef kabab from Saffy’s. Olivia Munn, Rachel Zoe and Julie Bowen Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Baby2Baby board member Julie Bowen and Malin Akerman led the fundraising portion — which resulted in a record-breaking over $18 million raised. Notable supporters like Paris Hilton and Jennifer Garner were among those making contributions. Alicia Keys Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Then, Alicia Keys honored athlete and entrepreneur Serena Williams with the Giving Tree Award. “We honor Serena for her fierce commitment to uplifting children and families with her powerful advocacy for maternal health,” Keys said. Williams spoke of her personal struggles in her acceptance speech. “When I had my daughter Olympia, I faced life-threatening complications,” she said. “I had access. I had privilege. But I wasn’t listened to. I wasn’t believed. And I came painfully close to losing everything.” Prince Harry and Meghan Markle flank honoree Serena Williams. Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby The experience changed her life: “It opened my eyes to the harsh reality that Black women are three times more likely to die from pregnancy-related causes,” Williams said. “That’s why Baby2Baby’s maternal health [effort] in addition to what they do for babies is so deeply personal to me: They distribute mental health and newborn supply kits … and postpartum care and vital educational resources precisely when the mom needs them.” Missy Elliott and Ciara Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby Jessica Alba and Ciara closed out the evening before a performance by musical guest, Ludacris — who got the crowd packed around the stage area and dancing to his hits, “All I Do Is Win,” “Stand Up,” and “Yeah!,” “Glamorous,” “How Low Can You Go” and “Shake Your Money Maker.” Kerry Washington and Camila Alves Credit: Getty Images for Baby2Baby An after-party DJed by DJ Nice continued to keep guests dancing — and eating, with pizzas by Jon & Vinny’s, PopUp Bagels and dessert items. Partygoers left with a bag of products from title sponsor Paul Mitchell and Summer Fridays — plus pizza in a to-go box. Credit: Author Don’t keep it to yourself…share the love! Peacemaker has proven to be one of the finest DC productions of all time. Shows like Lanterns , Booster Gold , and Paradise Lost are all part of the DCU lineup. Additionally, fans can expect Season 2 of Creature Commandos sometime in 2026. However, Gunn isn't just interested in his own work. Even though the DC Studios co-chair spent several years working for Marvel Studios, he enjoys watching DC characters on the small screen. Via several interviews and social media posts, Gunn has recommended a few shows because of their overall brilliance and the contribution they made to his creative process. We wouldn’t be surprised if he revives some of them down the line. 7 'Doom Patrol' (2019 – 2023) Riley Shanahan as Cliff Steele in Doom Patrol Max Doom Patrol centers on a team of misfit superheroes , each a victim of an accident that gave them special abilities. Led by the mysterious scientist, Dr. Niles Caulder (Timothy Dalton), the group includes Cyborg (Joivan Wade), Elasti-Woman (April Bowlby), Robotman (Brendan Fraser), Negative Man (Matt Bomer), and Crazy Jane (Diane Guerrero). Gunn Loves Ensembles Back in 2022, a fan popped a question on X , asking James Gunn: “Have you seen Doom Patrol ? If so, did you like it?” The director gave a short answer, simply saying. “Yes!” Knowing Gunn, he would have ignored the question if he didn’t like the show. It’s easy to see why he likes it. Gunn has always adored superhero squads more than individuals. This particular series is also full of eccentric characters (the kind he likes). Additionally, it thrives on meta humor, absurd storytelling, and uncensored moments — things he tends to appreciate. If the series hadn’t been made already, Gunn might have included the team in his new DCU franchise. But anything is possible, given that the Max project isn’t strongly tied to other old shows. Rita Farr, Jane, Vic Stone, Larry Trainor, and Cliff Steele make cameo appearances in “Crisis of Infinite Earths,” but that’s just about it. Trainor, Steele, and Farr also appear in Titans , but these were revealed to be variants. 6 'Harley Quinn' (2019 – present) HBO Max Harley Quinn (Kaley Cuoco) is struggling to cope after her breakup with the Joker (Alan Tudyk). She thus vows to topple him from the position of Gotham’s top villain. Quickly, Harley forms a crew that includes Rogue’s Gallery members like Poison Ivy (Lake Bell), King Shark (Ron Funches), Clayface (Alan Tudyk), and Doctor Psycho (Tony Hale). How will they fare in Harley Quinn ? A Refreshing Change in the Hierarchy Gunn has frequently mentioned Harley Quinn , praising it for its sharp humor, violence, and character development. Back in 2020, he even rallied his followers to watch the show to ensure it got another season. "Let's hope. Everyone watch Harley Quinn on @hbomax and help get them a well-deserved season three!" he posted on X . Well, the animated gem did indeed get a third season, with Gunn even making a cameo as himself. "We knew he was a fan of the show. He had sort of just, out of the blue, been tweeting about the show, clips, or just thoughts on it — all very positive," producer Patrick Schumaker told Insider . Speaking of cameos, the show really thrives from strong performances, thanks to a strong supporting cast that also includes Giancarlo Esposito and Tom Hollander. 5 'Supergirl' (2015 – 2021) The CW Supergirl is the story of the Kryptonian Kara Zor-El, aka, Kara Denvers (Melissa Benoist), who juggles between working as a reporter (like her more famous cousin Kal-El/Clark Kent) and protecting National City from nefarious figures. Early in the series, we learn that Kara was actually the first of her kind to be sent to Earth and was meant to protect her baby cousin, Kal-El, only for her spaceship to be knocked off course. When she finally arrived, Kal-El had already grown into Superman. An Important Part of the Foundation James Gunn has lauded The CW’s Supergirl several times, with his most recent words of adoration coming only a few weeks ago. "10 years ago today, the Supergirl pilot aired. It laid the blueprint for so much of what we’re doing in the DCU – a world where kindness, hope, and positive change are possible. Melissa Benoist was incredible," he posted on X . In another conversation with Entertainment Weekly , Gunn revealed that he had always wanted a Superman who was charming and awkward, and Melissa Benoist’s Kara was a huge inspiration. " Supergirl proved you could do earnest heroism without being cynical, and that’s the heart of our new DC." Additionally, in a Threads post referring to the Arrowverse series, Gunn says he enjoyed “the way they handled alien heritage, family, and finding your place in the world.” The show aside, Gunn clearly loves the character, hence the reason he has made a Kara Zor-El movie one of his top priorities . And he sure has great taste for loving the CW series as it has all the tasty ingredients likely appeal to fans of Superman mythos. It has well-choreographed action, magnificent villains, and a progressive tone, emphasizing the need for more opportunities for women in the workplace. 4 'Watchmen' (2019) Louis Gossett Jr as a frightened Will Reeves in Watchmen HBO Set 34 years after the events of the iconic ‘80s comic of the same name, Watchmen covers racist violence in modern-day Tulsa, Oklahoma. Here, a white supremacist known as the Seventh Kavalry has declared war on the Tulsa Police Department, forcing law enforcement officers to conceal their faces with masks. Enter Detective Sister Night (Regina King), who craves revenge for the deaths of her friend and the police chief. One of the Best Elseworlds Projects When asked about potential DCU plans for Watchmen on the Happy Sad Podcast , Gunn implied that anything is possible, declaring that he “did love the TV show." In a 2022 Escapist Magazine interview , the DC Studios co-chair also described the original comic as his "favorite comic book runs" and "one of my favorite works of art, period." Fans thus have every reason to stay positive. Even though Damon Lindelof — known for his work in Lost and Mrs. Davis — chose not to do a second season, it would be great for the Emmy-winning show (a whopping 11 statuettes) to continue because of its timely and socially relevant topics. Its coverage of racial prejudice and the criminal justice system is simply brilliant. Regina King’s performance also helps make this the best Watchmen production out of them all. 3 'Smallville' (2001 – 2011) Smallville The CW Smallville is about the coming-of-age adventures of a young Clark Kent (Tom Welling) in his hometown of Smallville, Kansas, before he becomes Superman. The first four seasons cover his high school life, his romance with Lana Lang (Kristin Kreuk), and his love-hate relationship with Lex Luthor (Michael Rosenbaum). From Season 5, Clark's early adult years play out, so Lois Lane (Erica Durance) and the Daily Planet come into the picture. That Essential Clark-Lex Dynamic In Superman , Lex Luthor’s company is called LuthorCorp , a name that only appears in the series and not the comics. A fan asked James Gunn about it on Threads , and he responded by saying that he indeed took the name from The CW show, declaring, “I’m a Smallville fan.” Proof of his love also comes from a 2023 post on X where he wrote, “Loved Smallville growing up. Tom and Michael had great chemistry.” Gunn’s Man of Steel movie proved that he cares a lot about the Clark-Lex dynamic. This is obviously a major reason why he loves the TV series, as the two characters really get on each other’s nerves numerous times. However, his love for the critically acclaimed small-screen production is also unusual, considering that he is never really a fan of origin stories. Most of his superhero movies directly introduce audiences to the adult versions of the characters. 2 'Batman: The Animated Series' (1992) Batman fighting The Joker while the Joker holds a long weapon in Batman: The Animated Series. Warner Bros. Animation Batman: The Animated Series follows Bruce Wayne/Batman (Kevin Conroy) as he protects Gotham City from the numerous criminals that roam in the underworld. Making great use of brains, martial arts skills, and high-tech gadgets, the Dark Knight battles iconic foes like The Joker (Mark Hamill), Two-Face (Richard Moll), and The Penguin (Paul Williams). Setting the Bar Gunn has never stopped talking about the show. In an X post in 2023, he declared that BTAS was “one of the best animated series of all time,” adding, “Kevin Conroy and Mark Hamill? Unbeatable.” The filmmaker goes deeper in a 2024 Collider interview. “The noir style, the voice acting, the way it treated mythology with respect and creativity — that’s the gold standard for DC animation.” Commenting on Threads after Kevin Conroy’s passing, Gunn also reminded everyone that thus “wasn’t just a kids’ show — it was art. Dark, emotional, beautiful.” The filmmaker’s take is spot on. A flawless show, BTAS has first-rate dialogue, stories, art design, and voice acting. Mark Hamill is especially a standout as the Joker. The orchestrated soundtrack is simply brilliant, too. Deservedly, the series won the Emmy Award for Outstanding Animated Programming. 1 'Justice League Unlimited' (2004 – 2006) The Question confronts Superman in Justice League Unlimited Warner Bros. Justice League Unlimited follows the titular team on numerous cosmic and city-related adventures . The members include Batman (Kevin Conroy), Superman (George Newbern), Wonder Woman (Susan Eisenberg), Flash (Michael Rosenbaum), Green Lantern (Phil LaMarr), Hawkgirl (Maria Canals-Barrera), and several others. How to Accommodate a Large Crowd Properly When an X user asked Gunn about animated influences in the DCU, he quickly mentioned JLU . “The way it handled big teams, personal stakes, and real moral questions — that’s the blueprint for what we’re doing with ensembles,” he said. The filmmaker reiterated his remarks in a CBR interview, stating that the show’s character arcs, depth, and continuity are what he wants for the DCU. There’s also a Thread post where Gunn says that JLU “knew how to land emotional punches without sacrificing fun.” As someone seeking to build a large universe, it makes sense for Gunn to love the most continuity-heavy show of the DC Animated Universe. The popular series effortlessly weaves together characters and plot lines from numerous past series, all while serving epic battles and exploring themes like loyalty, heroism, sacrifice, and moral quagmires. The one-hour variety special, a combination of music, comedy and fun celebrity testimonials, explores the issues and solutions for getting women back to work. The show will air on The CW Network on Wednesday, August 26 (8:00-9:00pm ET) and then move to The CW digital platforms, CWTV.COM and The CW App. Talent confirmed for the special thus far include Mara Brock Akil, Lake Bell, Alison Brie, Connie Britton, Nkechi Okoro Carroll, Rosario Dawson, Beanie Feldstein, Jane Fonda, Jennifer Garner, Elizabeth Gillies, Kathryn Hahn, Rachael Harris, Cheryl Hines, Sarah Jeffery, Marta Kauffman, Javicia Leslie, Melanie Liburd, Catt Sadler, Andrea Savage, Alexandra Shipp, Rain Valedz, Michaela Watkins, Kym Whitley, Alfre Woodard and others to be announced. The show’s executive producers are Stephanie Allain (“Dear White People,” the 2020 Academy Awards), Amy Baer (“Last Vegas”) and Monica Levinson (“Borat”). The directors are Hannah Levy (“Saturday Night Live”) and Adriana Robles (“Saturday Night Live”). The writers are Wendy Button (CNN’s “Heroes”), Simbi Hall (Women That Soar Awards) and Mishy Turner (“Unbreakable Kimmy Schmidt”). Hire Her Back (HHB) was launched on June 10, 2020 as a call for industry-wide action to rebuild a workforce that hires women and people of color equitably as we recover from the COVID-19 crisis. COVID-19 is both a public health pandemic and a socioeconomic crisis. Women and people of color are at a higher risk of job loss and of exposure to the virus. There is ample evidence suggesting that women will have significant difficulty rebounding from the COVID-19 crisis, in particular Latinx and Black women, who have faced some of the highest rates of unemployment of any group as a result of the pandemic. The goal is to protect the progress that women and people of color have made recently in front of and behind the camera: so that employers across the entertainment landscape hire women and people of color back to their former positions AND to fill new ones, to build to a new normal for parity in the screen industries. See also Shark Week 2023 Preview The additional goal is to raise money for the WIF Hire Her Back Fund that will disburse grants to women whose livelihoods in film and television have been adversely affected by the COVID-19 crisis as they are returning to the workforce. Funds raised will also be used to protect WIF’s core programs, which have been lifelines during the COVID-19 crisis. These include career pipeline and mentorship programs like INSIGHT, a collective of emerging BIWOC filmmakers, our Help Line for sexual harassment—which is expanding to address racial discrimination—as well as support groups for community members affected by the COVID-19 pandemic. While this will be WIF’s first televised benefit, its Annual Gala is covered by major media nationally and internationally. For the past 30+ years, WIF has produced a high-level annual live event that celebrates the achievement of women in film and television and has served as a platform to deliver key messages about gender equality and parity in front of and behind the camera. Last year’s show honored Issa Rae and Amy Poehler. Past honorees include Elizabeth Banks, Ava DuVernay, Nicole Kidman, Kerry Washington, Cate Blanchett, Laura Linney, Viola Davis, Annette Bening, Jennifer Aniston, Renée Zellweger, Jennifer Lopez, Sandra Bullock, Gwyneth Paltrow, Halle Berry, Glenn Close, Jessica Lange, Drew Barrymore, Meryl Streep, Angela Bassett, and many more. The special will be produced in association with ShivHans Pictures. Seed funding for the grants has been generously provided by the founder of ShivHans, producer Shivani Rawat. Additional contributions to the fund can be made at wif.org ; information about the grants is now available on the website. See also MeTV Remembers Dustin Diamond Founded in 1973 as Women In Film, Los Angeles, WIF advocates for and advances the careers of women working in the screen industries—to achieve parity and transform culture. Joshua Brown Updated: Nov 21, 2025 Where Winds Meet What regions are on the Where Winds Meet map? The Where Winds Meet map below splits key locations into its two main regions, which are then further split across six subdivisions or prefectures. This map can at least point you in the right direction if a character is requesting your presence somewhere you've yet to visit. With unlocks like the Panacea Fan being found in a specific area, a handy list of Where Winds Meet map locations can come in clutch. And if multiplayer is your aim, here's how to unlock co-op in Where Winds Meet , too. Where Winds Meet map Like most living open-world games these days, the Where Winds Meet map is set to expand over time, with the world map growing to contain more regions with new quests, chests, and unlocks. With another subdivision left shrouded in darkness in the upper corner of Keifeng, there's set to be much more to see and do as your young master helps out around the land. Where Winds Meet is currently made up of two large-scale regions: the northern stretch of Qinghe and the southern land of Kaifeng and Kaifeng City. Here's a look at the two major launch regions and the key locations that breathe life into this rendition of 10th-century China. Qinghe Made up of the Verdant Wilds to the east, Sundara Land to the north, and Moonveil Mountains to the west, the region of Qinghe is the home of your ancient hero. Verdant Wilds Comprised of the conflict-broken forts of the Battlecrest Slope as well as the reclaimed pagoda and huts of the Bamboo Abode and General's Shrine, the Stonewash Strand area of the Verdant Wilds is one area that's largely untouched. Verdant Wilds POIs Bamboo Abode Battlecrest Slope Stonewash Strand General's Shrine Crimson Cliff Sundara Land Head north, and you'll soon cross the river splitting Sundara Land from the rest of the Qinghe locale. This rocky region is flanked by the Jadebrook Mountain, with the Flower Expanse punctuating the crossing between the Blissful Retreat. With multiple residential areas, big and small, scattered around the peaks, Sundara Land is a picturesque land of mystery and intrigue. Sundara Land POIs Buddha Fort Wildmane Ranch Finesteed Hamlet Bodhi Sea Jadebrook Mountain Flower Expanse Mercyheart Town Halo Peak Thousand-Buddha Village Mercyheart Monastery Floral Expanse Beyond Moonveil Mountains Home to important early locations in our protagonist's life, like Still Shore and Harvestfall Village. You can't make your way to the southern land of Kaifeng without taking in the sights and sounds of the areas comprising the Moonveil Mountains. The eastern side hides the Gleaming Abyss in plain view, with small abodes covertly scattered throughout the surrounding Witherwilds, offering a genuine sense of adventure along the straight roads. Stick to the path and you'll come across Riverside Station. Take a wrong turn in life and you'll wind up there by someone else's hand. Rest easy around the Velvet Shade, or take in the true nature of the ancient metropolis by visiting Prosperity Haven and the Imperial Artisan Court. As the sun sets over the cloud-covered pagoda, end the day on a high with the many joys to be had around the Fairgrounds area. Hard work can be found around the towering Furnace Area, and you can take in the darker side of town by hitting up the Ghostlight Market and Unbound Cavern. The Masterwood Hamlet and Buddha Statue Sites showcase the craftsmanship of Kaifeng's top artisans, with the vast Imperial Garden bringing collective opulence to the region. The East and South Kaifeng Suburbs show the hopeful side of the less prosperous section of the Kaifeng City region. The marsh of Mistveil Forest and the rolling hills of Plainfield perfectly punctuate the hard-working attitude that goes into keeping the Ever-Normal Granary powering the whole region. text: Vogue World and Swarovski Honor Hollywood Skip to content Subscribe Main Navigation TV TV Ratings Reviews Movies Movies Steve Pond Reviews Box Office Venice Film Festival Report From Toronto Sundance Sundance Videos Cannes Cannes Magazine CinemaCon Awards Visionaries Awards Emmys Oscars How I Did It Venice Film Festival WrapStyle WrapStyle Homepage TheWrapBook Volume 4: The Art of Television 2025 TheWrapBook Volume 3: The Art of Cinema TheWrapBook Volume 2: The Art of Television TheWrapBook Volume 1: The Art of Cinema PRO Members Hub Data Insights Streaming Charts Waxword The Media Front Game On: A Wrap Sports Series The Grill WrapPRO What to Watch More Media Tech The Media Front Power Women Summit Screening Series RSVP Screenings Archive How She Did It How I Did It Digital Covers Newsletters Newsletters Search Search The Wrap Search Subscribe Follow Us Visit The Wrap on facebook Visit The Wrap on twitter Visit The Wrap on instagram Visit The Wrap on youtube Vogue World and Swarovski Honor Hollywood Costume’s Influence; Fashion’s FYC Season WrapStyle: This year’s Vogue event was a flex for the magazine and a long-overdue recognition of the influence film has on fashion Booth Moore October 31, 2025 @ 3:27 PM Share on Social Media Share on Facebook Share on X (formerly Twitter) Share on LinkedIn Share on Email Nicole Kidman walks the runway during Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26. Source: Getty Vogue World: Hollywood was a flex for the magazine and a long-overdue recognition of the influence film has on fashion. Also, Swarovski’s must-see “Masters of Light: Hollywood” exhibition of fashion and costume is on display and open to the public until Nov. 3. Greta Lee walks the runway during Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty Vogue World: Hollywood Is a Rah-Rah for the Fashion and Film Industries With Paramount Studios serving as a runway stage, Baz Luhrmann directing, a Chanel-clad Nicole Kidman starring, and a stacked celebrity cast and front row, Vogue World: Hollywood was a joyous mashup of fashion and film, featuring iconic Hollywood costumes, characters, fresh-off-the-runway fashion and archival looks. Say what you will about it being a pointless marketing exercise, and many online have said exactly that, but it was a rah-rah for both struggling industries, and a flex for Vogue, which is the only brand on the planet that could have pulled in all that star power. It also raised $4.5 million for the Entertainment Community Fund, providing a safety net for arts workers hit particularly hard this year. Sunday’s event brought 400-plus guests to the Paramount lot, including what were surely the most famous extras in history. “Picture’s up, places please, picture’s up!” a stage manager called over the bullhorn as they arrived on set. Miley Cyrus, Hailey Bieber and Anthony Vaccarello attend Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty “They’re stressing everybody out because we all actually do this and when you say picture’s up it’s serious!” Miley Cyrus said, walking in incognito wearing a Saint Laurent leather trench, newsboy cap and sunglasses. “I’m looking for the next motion picture star!” stylist Brad Goreski joked, looking every bit the studio boss in a dapper suit, sunglasses and slicked-back hair, arriving with Ashley Park in a corseted Wiederhoeft dress that carried a sense of costume. Brad Goreski and Ashley Park attend Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty Stars from music (Rita Ora, V, Machine Gun Kelly, Lizzo), film (Dakota Johnson, Gwyneth Paltrow, Cynthia Erivo, Taika Waititi), costume (Sandy Powell, Ruth E. Carter, Colleen Atwood), fashion (Anthony Vaccarello, Zac Posen, Jerry Lorenzo) and other power players in Anna Wintour’s orbit (Gov. Gavin Newsom, Bryan Lourd, Tyler Perry, Casey Wasserman) strolled past props, costume rails and spotlights on their way to director’s chair seats. The runway was high-energy and fast — people were having fun! — which is something we need more of in fashion and worked well for the 35-minute livestream of the show. While it was confusing to figure out what was designer-made and what was costume, that may have been the point. Damson Idris and Angela Bassett walk the runway at Vogue World: Hollywood 2025 at Paramount Studios on Oct. 26, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. Source: Getty The art forms have blurred. Costume designers have dipped their toes into fashion design and collaborated with luxury brands on films, not to mention continually influencing runway and street style decade after decade. Meanwhile, fashion designers are casting Hollywood faces as brand ambassadors, bringing even more showmanship to their runway shows and clothing to reach digital audiences, and even stepping into producing and costuming Hollywood films. All of it was on display on the runway. L.A.-based designers Kate and Laura Mulleavy were working in both worlds long before Anthony Vaccarello and Saint Laurent Films began producing awards-contending movies. They designed costumes for the 2010 film “Black Swan,” have cited the influence of films including “Suspiria” and “Star Wars” on many of their runway collections over the years, and made their own 2017 feature film, “Woodshock.” So it was fitting that several of their looks appeared on the Vogue World runway. Kendall Jenner wears a costume from “Moulin Rouge!,” a model wears a dress by Rodarte, Doja Cat wears a costume by Michael Schmidt inspired by Tina Turner in “Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome.” Source: Getty There used to be more of an impervious line between Hollywood costume and fashion; costume was for character building and serving a script, fashion was purely commercial. But all that’s gone out the window, as the relationship between Hollywood and fashion has become symbiotic. “In this era, people are able to step out of the boxes more and interact in the two fields simultaneously, and it’s accepted and celebrated,” Laura Mulleavy told me, noting that it was another polymath, Shirley Kurata, their longtime runway stylist and the costume designer for the 2022 film “Everything Everywhere All At Once,” who curated the evening’s contemporary character costumes. Jeff Goldblum walks the runway wearing Gucci at Vogue World. Source: Getty This recognition of costume designers’ contributions to visual culture — and to fashion, including countless collection mood boards — was long overdue. I can’t tell you how many times I’ve previewed a collection with a fashion designer who talks about being inspired by a particular film without naming, or even knowing, the costume designer. Hopefully, that mindset will start to change. The photo below says it all about the flow of creativity and reference from one world to the other — Wintour poses with costume designer Mona May and her iconic yellow plaid suit, as worn by Alicia Silverstone in the 1995 film “Clueless,” alongside a checked suit in the same spirit by fashion designer Thom Browne. Left to right, a model wears Thom Browne, costume designer Mona May, Condé Nast Chief Content Director Anna Wintour and a Mona May-designed costume from Clueless. Source: Getty There was a lot to look at on the runway. Some of the highlights: Kendall Jenner as a “Moulin Rouge!” showgirl in a leggy look from costume designer Catherine Martin, and “Great Gatsby” flappers — including Elizabeth Debicki — wearing beaded gowns Martin created for the 2013 film in collaboration with Prada. The tribute to the late, great style icon Diane Keaton and her influential “Annie Hall” look was not only touching but telling of how costume and fashion can intersect. It was originally developed by Keaton in 1977 with costume designer Ruth Morley, using some pieces from her personal wardrobe and some from Ralph Lauren, who recreated the look for the runway here, and has referenced it many times in his fashion collections over the years. There were also homages to the unforgettable costumes of “The Royal Tenenbaums” (Karen Patch), “Once Upon a Time in Hollywood” (Arianne Phillips) and “Edward Scissorhands” (Colleen Atwood). Elizabeth Debicki wallks the runway at Vogue World. Source: Getty Angela Bassett closed the Afrofuturism section looking regal in her Ruth E. Carter gown on the heels of dancing “Black Panther” Wakandan warriors. Greta Lee worked a theatrical look and tricorne hat from fashion/costume designer Jonathan Anderson’s first Dior collection shown just weeks ago. Jeff Goldblum owned his Gucci sequin jacket and his runway walk, and Julia Garner skipped down the runway as the picture of baroque frivolity in a Milena Canonero for “Marie Antoinette” costume. Julia Garner walks the runway at Vogue World. Source: Getty Gracie Abrams played the part of Chanel ambassador, performing in a fresh-off-the-runway look by Matthieu Blazy, while Doja Cat shook her hips in a chainmail dress inspired by Tina Turner in “Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome,” but executed by L.A.’s Michael Schmidt, a too-often unsung hero of costume design and fabrication. It was a blast and nobody wanted it to end. On the way out, I ran into “Frankenstein” costume designer Kate Hawley, whose ravishing work, including curating Tiffany & Co. archival jewels and custom pieces for the film, is proof that the love affair between costume and fashion isn’t ending anytime soon. Costume designers Mona May, Sandy Powell, Catherine Martin, Ruth E. Carter, Arianne Phillips, Milena Canonero, Jacqueline West, Shirley Kurata with Anna Wintour at Vogue World: Hollywood. Source: Getty Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood” Source: Swarovski Fashion’s FYC Season Brands have descended on L.A. in what I’m calling fashion’s FYC (For Your Consideration) period in the lead-up to awards season. Everything from Boucheron jewels and hot-off-the-runway Versace to designer Camilla Franks’ fun, rock ’n’ roll resortwear and Le Monde Beryl’s red-carpet-ready silk pumps is being showcased for celebrities and stylists at spectacular events, rented hotel rooms and showrooms across the city. The goal? To create media moments, build relationships and make deals as opportunities to dress up, ramp up over the next few months. Swarovski joined the chorus Tuesday, asserting its role as chief embellisher of fashion and film. Global creative director Giovanna Engelbert and CEO Alexis Nasard hosted the opening of the Swarovski “Masters of Light” immersive exhibition — following stops in Vienna, Milan, Shanghai and Seoul — curated by Alexander Fury with a Hollywood focus for this edition. Unlike most fashion happenings, this is open to the public, through Nov. 3 in the former Amoeba Music space. Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie designed gown worn by Marilyn Monroe on display at Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood.” Source: Swarovski Cher, Viola Davis, Kylie Jenner, Elizabeth Olsen, Jeff Goldblum and many more turned out for the sparkly opening, exploring galleries showcasing Swarovski’s 130 year history of bedazzling fashion, jewelry, home decor and more. The brand has a century-long history in Hollywood, from lighting up Dorothy’s ruby red slippers in “The Wizard of Oz” (there’s a pair in the exhibition), to creating the jewels worn by Marilyn Monroe in “Gentlemen Prefer Blondes” (also here), to partnering with the Academy Awards, and on many a costume and red carpet dress. Like Vogue World, the exhibition is a conversation between fashion and costume — and full of eye candy — including the Jean-Louis and Bob Mackie-designed nude illusion dress worn by Monroe when she sang “Happy Birthday” to President John F. Kennedy, and by Kim Kardashian to the Met Gala, which had its own velvet-roped vestibule. Cher and Giovanna Battaglia Engelbert at the opening of Swarovski “Masters of Light: Hollywood.” Source: Swarovski Demonstrating how costumes have inspired fashion, Travis Banton’s gold silk, glass bead, bullion, crystal and mink “Fabergé” dress — said to be one of the most expensive ever produced by Paramount and worn by Marlene Dietrich in the 1937 film “Angel” — is displayed next to a 2024 Marc Jacobs gown inspired by it. “Masters of Light” offers a window into the brand’s craft and design process in vivid color, and many more show stopping looks, including Josephine Baker’s incredible metal and crystal bra and feather costume from “La Revue Nègre,” Katy Perry’s iconic Jeremy Scott chandelier dress, a crystallized Harry Styles jumpsuit and more worn by Cher, Madonna, Grace Jones, Beyoncé, Tina Turner, Carey Mulligan and more. Tickets can be purchased here . Left, Travis Banton’s “Fabergé” dress from the 1937 film Angel, and right, the 2024 Marc Jacobs dress it inspired. Source: Swarovski Valérie Messika and Orlando Bloom at the Messika celebratory dinner at The Frick Collection in New York. Source: Messika Sparkling from Coast to Coast Meanwhile in New York, Messika jewelry celebrated its 20th anniversary, and the opening of a new Madison Avenue flagship, with a glittering dinner at The Frick Collection bringing together a cross-section of celebrities, fashion insiders and friends of the brand. More than 120 guests, including Julianne Moore, Charlotte Lawrence, Nina Dobrev, Kiko Mizuhara, Orlando Bloom, and Gunna, gathered in the museum’s galleries for an evening that blended haute joaillerie and haute cuisine. In a clever twist, models dressed as servers and glided through the dining room in a trompe-l’œil performance, revealing Messika’s high jewelry pieces as they moved. Messika celebratory dinner at The Frick Collection in New York City. Source: Messika The centerpiece was the So Move Rainbow High Jewelry set, with 24 sapphire shades and rubies created exclusively for the new boutique. Rainbow hues ran throughout the event — from the photo call backdrop to the table settings to the anniversary cake. Produced by We Are Ona, known for its immersive culinary events, the dinner featured a custom menu by Chef Alexia Duchêne, and culminated in a soulful performance by Toni Braxton. “This opening is more than a milestone,” Valérie Messika, who founded the modern jewelry brand in Paris in 2005, said. “It’s a bridge between Paris and New York, between savoir-faire and emotion, and the beginning of a luminous new chapter for Messika in the United States.” Laura Brown, Laura Dern, Kristina O’Neill and Cindy Crawford celebrate “All The Cool Girls Get Fired” at the Tory Burch store. Source: Tory Burch All The Cool Girls… Former magazine editors Laura Brown and Kristina O’Neill have been crisscrossing the country with their new book, “All The Cool Girls Get Fired,” which I had the pleasure of interviewing them about onstage at Reese Witherspoon’s Shine Away event a couple weekends back. It’s a timely read for people who, ahem, have been laid off, with personal anecdotes from Oprah, Katie Couric, Jamie Lee Curtis and others, as well as practical advice about COBRA and mental health — all the fun stuff. Zoey Deutch, Jurnee Smollett and Monica Lewinsky read excerpts from “All the Cool Girls Get Fired.” Source: Tory Burch The authors were back in L.A. last week for a party at the Tory Burch store where Kiernan Shipka, Lake Bell, Jurnee Smollett and others took turns reading excerpts from the book. Monica Lewinsky stole the show, however, with her introduction: “I don’t mean to show anyone up, but I was fired from the White House!” I asked guests for their getting-fired stories. Burch has never been fired (of course she hasn’t). Cindy Crawford was asked to leave a Bruce Weber shoot once, but models don’t get fired so much as they don’t get booked, she said. Stylist/manager/producer Jeanne Yang was fired from her job as a salesperson in the Bullocks Wilshire lingerie department way back when, which led her to Details magazine and eventually to styling—a good thing in retrospect. A setback that was really a setup, as they say. Cheers to that. Forwarded this newsletter? Subscribe here to get WrapStyle directly every week! Have a news story for our readers? text: Jamie Chung on Her, Bryan Greenberg's Twin Sons Time in the NICU News Photos Videos Black Friday Deals Kardashians Royals TV Scoop News Photos Videos Black Friday Deals Kardashians Royals TV Scoop Exclusive How Jamie Chung and Bryan Greenberg Navigated Their Twins' Time in the NICU Jamie Chung, who has partnered with Carter's, spoke exclusively to E! News about how she and husband Bryan Greenberg navigated their twins' time in the NICU. By Sabba Rahbar , Kristina Behr Nov 17, 2025 4:00 PM | Updated Nov 17, 2025 6:31 PM Tags Babies Interviews Exclusives Celeb Kids Jamie Chung Celebrities LINK COPIED! Watch : How Jamie Chung and Bryan Greenberg Navigated Their Twins' Time in the NICU Jamie Chung knows firsthand how difficult the first days of motherhood can be. And the Big Hero 6 actress and husband Bryan Greenberg had an especially tough time as their now 4-year-old twin boys spent their first weeks in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) after they were born prematurely. “One had a two-week stint and then graduated,” Jamie shared in an exclusive interview with E! News. “Our other child was there for a week.” And as the 42-year-old explained, it was a “really scary experience” for both her and Bryan, 47, as they were first time parents holding their boys who were barely four pounds. “You're hearing the heart rate monitors and seeing all these incubators,” Jamie recalled, “and what a wonderful thing to have these wonderful NICU nurses hold your hand through this entire experience, because it can be quite traumatizing.” For the former reality star and her husband of 10 years, it really was just them and the NICU nurses navigating the experience together because their family wasn’t able to visit. read Why Jamie Chung Says the Hardest Phase of Motherhood Was the Beginning “Another great support were our friends,” Jamie added , including one pal who works as a NICU nurse and was "a great resource” for their questions . Looking back on it now, she is still “eternally grateful” for the care she and her family received in the hospital . Joey Andrew The experience has led Jamie to partner with Carter’s Charitable Foundation , which is donating $50,000 to March of Dimes during National Prematurity Awareness Month in November to help raise awareness about premature birth and support families who are navigating their own NICU journeys. “[March of Dimes is] a great organization that ensures the overall health and safety for all moms and premature babies,” Jamie shared . “It’s pretty incredible.” Her time with her babies in the NICU also made her realize how important it is to have well-designed clothes for premature infants, which inspired another part of the clothing company's philanthropic work. “For the last 20 years, Carter's has collaborated with NICU nurses and families on design,” Jamie explained , “like little kimonos and caps that make it a lot easier for the caretakers as well as NICU nurses.” CraSH/Shutterstock “As our children got bigger, accessibility is everything,” Jamie continued . “When you're changing a blowout, you got to have the zipper.” And her children have certainly gotten bigger, with Jamie telling E! it happened in the blink of an eye. “All of a sudden , they go from four pounds to 40,” she shared. “They really do grow up so fast.” The Once Upon a Time actress is now doing her best to appreciate every moment , because she was so overwhelmed during the baby stage and couldn’t enjoy it as thoroughly. “I was just on survival mode—burping, feeding, changing. It was really overwhelming,” she recounted. “But now I really make it a point to be present instead of rushing.” She added, “It’s been a great joy and delight.” For the latest breaking news updates, click here to download the E! The latest movie to come from Vertical also serves as the first foray into feature-length filmmaking for its helmer, Sophie Tabet , who has previously backed shorts including The Lonely Whale and Croque Monsieur . With a co-starring performance from Kiernan Shipka ( Chilling Adventures of Sabrina ), the movie centers around one young woman’s attempt to break free from a crime-driven cult led by a ruthless queenpin known as Goldie (Ritter). Set for a cinematic arrival on November 7, the movie packs a classic ‘80s crime thriller punch with some serious star power and engaging storyline to boot. Breakfast is incredibly tense in our new look at Stone Cold Fox , where Ritter’s Goldie sits at the head of the table and addresses her followers. As the group sips their orange juice and gleefully digs into the bacon and eggs that sit at the center of the table, Goldie catches the others up on their latest “lucrative deal,” promising them that by next week, they’ll have “a real pool” on the compound. Vibes are high, as the members beam from ear to ear and high-five one another thanks to the good news just as Goldie asks them to raise a glass to toast the memory of her father — who taught her everything she knows about the business. The touching moment is quickly interrupted by Fox (Shipka), who sits to Goldie’s right, when she makes a joke that rubs the dangerous leader the wrong way and is quickly reminded why Goldie is the queenpin that she’s become. Joining Ritter and Shipka in this fun, colorful, and thrilling throwback to our favorite action genre of the past is a magnificent lineup that also includes Kiefer Sutherland ( The Lost Boys ), Karen Fukuhara ( The Boys ), Jamie Chung ( Sucker Punch ), Mishel Prada ( The Continental ), Gabrielle Maiden ( The Electric State ), Spenser Granese ( Better Call Saul ) and more. What Is ‘Stone Cold Fox’ About? Seeking care and community in all the wrong places , Fox (Shipka) finds herself involved with Goldie’s (Ritter) gang of criminals . As our sneak peek unveiled, whatever warm and snuggly feelings were once plentiful between the leader and follower eventually run their course, and Fox looks for a way out. Upon finding her exit, Fox digs up numerous piles of cash that Goldie’s been storing underground and makes a break for it, only to find herself in even more trouble after she discovers that Goldie and her gang have kidnapped her younger sister. With no other choice, Fox walks directly into Goldie’s trap in hopes of saving her sibling and maybe even escaping with her own life. Check out our new look at Stone Cold Fox above and see it on November 7. With a co-starring performance from Kiernan Shipka ( Chilling Adventures of Sabrina ), the movie centers around one young woman’s attempt to break free from a crime-driven cult led by a ruthless queenpin known as Goldie (Ritter). Set for a cinematic arrival on November 7, the movie packs a classic ‘80s crime thriller punch with some serious star power and engaging storyline to boot. Breakfast is incredibly tense in our new look at Stone Cold Fox , where Ritter’s Goldie sits at the head of the table and addresses her followers. As the group sips their orange juice and gleefully digs into the bacon and eggs that sit at the center of the table, Goldie catches the others up on their latest “lucrative deal,” promising them that by next week, they’ll have “a real pool” on the compound. Vibes are high, as the members beam from ear to ear and high-five one another thanks to the good news just as Goldie asks them to raise a glass to toast the memory of her father — who taught her everything she knows about the business. The touching moment is quickly interrupted by Fox (Shipka), who sits to Goldie’s right, when she makes a joke that rubs the dangerous leader the wrong way and is quickly reminded why Goldie is the queenpin that she’s become. Joining Ritter and Shipka in this fun, colorful, and thrilling throwback to our favorite action genre of the past is a magnificent lineup that also includes Kiefer Sutherland ( The Lost Boys ), Karen Fukuhara ( The Boys ), Jamie Chung ( Sucker Punch ), Mishel Prada ( The Continental ), Gabrielle Maiden ( The Electric State ), Spenser Granese ( Better Call Saul ) and more. What Is ‘Stone Cold Fox’ About? Seeking care and community in all the wrong places , Fox (Shipka) finds herself involved with Goldie’s (Ritter) gang of criminals. As our sneak peek unveiled, whatever warm and snuggly feelings were once plentiful between the leader and follower eventually run their course, and Fox looks for a way out. Upon finding her exit, Fox digs up numerous piles of cash that Goldie’s been storing underground and makes a break for it, only to find herself in even more trouble after she discovers that Goldie and her gang have kidnapped her younger sister. With no other choice, Fox walks directly into Goldie’s trap in hopes of saving her sibling and maybe even escaping with her own life. News By MarkJulian - Nov 22, 2025 12:11 PM EST Filed Under: Netflix Source: Toonado.com Zack Snyder’s Twilight of the Gods wraps its first season on a major cliffhanger, but it appears Netflix has no plans to continue the story. According to a new report, the series has been cancelled, alongside Exploding Kittens and the animated reboot of Good Times . ‘Twilight of the Gods’, ‘Exploding Kittens’ and ‘Good Times’ have all been canceled after one season at Netflix. (Source: https://t.co/p9NJm21Xcg ) pic.twitter.com/fnUKiBUhQX — Cartoon Base (@TheCartoonBase) November 21, 2025 Season 1 of Twilight of the Gods ends with the revelation that Loki was secretly the mastermind behind the events that sent Sigrid on her quest of vengeance and with the death of Baldr triggering the beginning events of Ragnarök, it certainly seemed as if the stage was set for more episodes. However, according to What's On Netflix , the streamer has decided not to produce additional episodes of Snyder's animation project and the decision was based purely on viewership ratings. The show ultimately didn’t perform at the level Netflix had hoped on a global scale, an issue it shares with several other high-profile Snyder-led projects at the service. Snyder's other projects at the network, additional installments in the Army of the Dead and Rebel Moon universes, also appear to be dead in the water. His previously announced LAPD action thriller is also said to now be placed on the streamer's back burner. Circling back to Twilight of the Gods, the 8-episode project was a collaboration between Snyder's Stone Quarry Animation and the France-based Xilam Animation, with Jay Oliva serving as showrunner and Eric Carrasco positioned as head writer. Previously, Snyder said he and Oliva were keenly interested in making a second season, stating, "Yes, there’s a massive roadmap. We know exactly what will happen. It’s just a matter of seeing if there’s an appetite for it." But it doesn't look as if that's going to come to fruition, at least at Netflix. The full voice cast for Twilight of the Gods featured: Sylvia Hoeks (Blade Runner 2049) as SIGRID Stuart Martin (Army of Thieves) as LEIF Pilou Asbæk (Game of Thrones, Ghost in the Shell) as THOR John Noble (Lord of the Rings, Fringe) as ODIN Paterson Joseph (Timeless) as LOKI Rahul Kohli (Supergirl, iZombie) as EGILL Jamie Clayton (Sense8) as THE SEID-KONA Kristopher Hivju (Game of Thrones) as ANDVARI Peter Stormare (American Gods, Castlevania) as ULFR Jamie Chung (Sucker Punch, Lovecraft Country) as HEL Lauren Cohan (The Walking Dead) as INGE Corey Stoll (Ant-Man, The Strain) as HRAFNKEL In a mythical world of great battles, great deeds, and great despair, Leif (Stuart Martin), a mortal king, is saved on the battlefield by Sigrid (Sylvia Hoeks), an iron-willed warrior with whom he falls in love. On their wedding night, Sigrid and Leif survive a wrath of terror from Thor (Pilou Asbæk), which sets them — and a crew of crusaders — on a merciless mission for vengeance, against all odds. This heroic story of love, loss, and revenge, is a journey to hell and beyond … across fantastical lands, battlefields fierce and bloody, and wars waged against deities and demons. Très Gelée, meaning “very jelly” in French, is made entirely of silicone, making it wipeable and durable. “Fashion has always been my hobby, my escape,” said Mueller, whose path in fashion wasn’t conventional. With a background in television and entertainment, she first entered the product world through e-commerce before realizing her passion for accessories. “Even as a kid, I’d layer all my grandma’s jewelry and play dress-up for hours.” Related Articles Lifestyle At the Vegas Formula 1 Grand Prix, Moët, LVMH and Beyoncé Steal the Spotlight Fashion Scoops EXCLUSIVE: Jonathan Anderson to Show First Dior Cruise Collection in Los Angeles It wasn’t until her own handbags became the site of frequent lipstick explosions and snack spills that the idea for Très Gelée took shape. Silicone was the breakthrough. text: Stone Cold Fox Review: Tonally Inconsistent and Remarkably Generic Movies TV Reviews Trailers Originals search search Movies News Reviews Trailers Posters Release Dates Box Office Interviews Lists Originals Genres Action Horror Sci-Fi Thrillers Horror News Reviews Trailers Posters Upcoming Originals Interviews Video Games TV News Reviews Trailers Interviews Home Cinema 4K Blu-Ray DVD Home Theater Tech Collectibles Release Dates Theatrical Streaming 4K / Blu-Rays Celebrity Interviews Pop Culture Retro Anime Gaming About Us Movie Reviews Stone Cold Fox Review: Tonally Inconsistent and Remarkably Generic By Tyler Nichols Posted 3 weeks ago Last Updated on November 17, 2025 PLOT : In this ’80s revenge story, the defiant Fox breaks out of an abusive commune in search of her family. But when the queenpin kidnaps her little sister and sends a crooked cop after her, Fox has no choice but to infiltrate the very place she escaped. REVIEW : I always love a good crime film and have enjoyed Kiernan Shipka and Krysten Ritter for so long that Stone Cold Fox seemed like an ideal film for me. I also love a movie set in the 80s. Its plot is basic enough, with Fox (Shipka) stealing a duffel bag full of cocaine and trying to get away from her old life. Now her ex (and head of the criminal organization), Goldie, and a crooked Cop (Sutherland) are after her. They seemingly kidnap Fox’s sister and force her to confront her past. It’s a pretty run-of-the-mill story, but that’s not always a bad thing, especially when you have such a stellar cast. Shipka is a fun, albeit vanilla lead. Her only bit of drive is more reliant on the audience not knowing something, versus her actually having a proper mission. Krysten Ritter’s Goldie is manipulative and abusive, but fails to really make a massive impact. Ritter is a bit too over the top, and feels a tad miscast, as she’s not a very believable crime boss. So, Fox running away from her doesn’t feel very tense. sponsored content Kiefer Sutherland is the standout of the film, as his Sergeant Billy Breaker is one bad dude. He’s a racist and is extremely corrupt. As someone who grew up with Sutherland as Jack Bauer, I always enjoy it when he takes a more villainous role. The writing lets him down a bit, as Breaker is pretty one-note, but his scenes are easily the most intriguing. I liked Jamie Chung as Officer Corbett, a cop who is suspicious of Breaker and is hot on his trail. But she could have been cut, and very little of the story would have changed. Despite being set in the 80s, Stone Cold Fox tries to have this strange 60s/70s drug aesthetic at times. It’s got crazy tie-dye visuals, and even a bit of roller-skating disco. It feels like the editor is trying to add a bit of life to what is otherwise quite visually mundane. And there’s a persistent high grain filter that makes every shot look very soft. Many of the characters get an over-stylized introduction, which just adds to the odd tone of the film. Sophie Tabet makes her feature directorial debut with Stone Cold Fox , and it’s a rather sterile affair. None of the characters have much life to them, and it’s hard to take the film very seriously. There are too many detours from the main story to make it feel like the stakes are high enough. It’s tonally inconsistent, and something about the visual style really threw me off. And the ending is an incoherent mess that tries to neatly tie up all its plot threads in a bow, resulting in a lot of silliness and some truly head-scratching moments. Stone Cold Fox falls a bit on its face and, despite needing more personality to make it work, it’s all very generic. Nothing feels unique, and it’s all very “been there, done that.” Despite boasting a great cast, most of the characters blend together, and it can all be a bit nonsensical. It wants to be a cool crime thriller, but the poor writing prevents it from gaining any proper momentum. The cast does its best to elevate the material, but the short runtime prevents it from really grasping onto anything interesting. It lacks the crime element and tries to be quirky without understanding what that entails. Stone Cold Fox releases on November 7th, 2025 . Pictures By Collier Jennings Published 6 days ago Collier Jennings is an entertainment journalist with a substantial amount of experience under his belt. Collier, or "CJ" to his friends and family, is a dedicated fan of genre films - particularly science fiction, fantasy and comic book adaptations, not to mention all forms of animation animation. This stems from a close bond with his father, who introduced him to these genres via copies of X-Men comics and reruns of the original Ultraman series. Using his near-encyclopedic knowledge and bottomless love of genre, he's been able to tackle a wide variety of articles. Sign in to your Collider account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap When Zack Snyder 's name comes up in discussion, one of two things will happen. Some people will argue that he's a visionary director who's been unfairly maligned by critics and the Internet. Others feel his work is juvenile at best and, at worst, incredibly self-indulgent. Most of this discussion stems from the fact that Snyder's work often adapts pre-existing material, whether it's iconic comics like Watchmen and 300 or mythology in his Netflix series Twilight of the Gods . It's Snyder's first original film, Sucker Punch , that is receiving a new lease on life , breaking into the Top 10 on HBO Max this week , per FlixPatrol . Looking at any of the trailers or stills from Sucker Punch , it's not hard to see why it's a draw for HBO Max users. The film follows Babydoll ( Emily Browning ), a young woman who is falsely institutionalized for the murder of her sister. Intending to escape before she's lobotomized, she turns to the other patients for help: Rocket ( Jena Malone ) and her sister Sweet Pea ( Abbie Cornish ), Amber ( Jamie Chung ), and "Blondie" ( Vanessa Hudgens ). The five women embark on a journey through different fantasy worlds full of stone samurai, a train full of killer robots, and steam-powered Nazi zombies. If that wasn't enough, Babydoll also fantasizes that she and her newfound friends are dancers in a brothel, which looks and sounds like a hyper-stylized and hyper-violent take on Inception . It also bears all of Snyder's signature flourishes, including slo-mo fight scenes and visuals that tend to have more definition than the characters, so what went wrong the first time around? Zack Snyder Has Yet To Realize His True Vision for ‘Sucker Punch’ When Sucker Punch had its theatrical release in 2011, it was a critical punching bag and a box office bomb. Quentin Tarantino scathingly referred to it as " one of the worst films of 2011 ", while other reviews compared it to a bad video game despite Snyder's insistence he didn't want the film to play out like one . Yet Babydoll and her friends are sent on quests to find various items, hoping to achieve a "perfect victory" that sounds more like a video game. The kicker was the fate of the main characters; nearly all the main heroines are brutally killed or maimed, which didn't earn the film any favors . Yet as time has passed, Sucker Punch has gathered a cult following and has even been examined through the lens of satire . There might be an underlying reason Sucker Punch received such a poor reception: it's not the version of the film Snyder intended to show the world . While Sucker Punch would receive a director's cut in the vein of other Snyder films , he told Empire Magazine in an interview last year that he'd like the chance to re-edit the film to match his vision : "I have the footage already shot: they just have to let me put it together...We ask every now and then. We have to ask again. I think there has to be a window when no-one’s got the movie." Given that Snyder was eventually able to complete his version of Justice League , there's a possibility that lightning could strike twice in his favor. However, it all comes down to whether Warner Bros. Pictures is willing to pull the trigger and whether there's a similar demand for the "Snyder Cut" of Sucker Punch. Posts By Marcel Ardivan Apr 11, 2025 ‘Sucker Punch’ Was a Major Stepping Stone for One Actor Everett Collection One of the most impressive aspects of Sucker Punch , aside from its gorgeous visuals, is its stacked ensemble cast . In addition to the main heroines, Sucker Punch also features Jon Hamm , Carla Gugino , and Oscar Isaac in key roles. In the case of Isaac, he portrays Blue Jones, the main antagonist of Sucker Punch. Isaac's performance allows him to craft two different characters, as Blue's depicted as the owner of a brothel and a domineering orderly at the asylum; both are equally slimy. Isaac is often considered one of the best parts of Sucker Punch , and, thanks to that film and his appearance in Drive , 2011 was his breakout year, leading him to bigger and better performances, including Guillermo del Toro 's Frankenstein . Sucker Punch, in many ways, best defines Zack Snyder as a filmmaker . It is visually stunning and swings for the fences, but it is also extremely divisive. Now that it's made the top 10 charts on HBO Max, a whole new audience will have the chance to decide whether it's a misunderstood masterpiece or a major misfire. Using his near-encyclopedic knowledge and bottomless love of genre, he's been able to tackle a wide variety of articles. Some people will argue that he's a visionary director who's been unfairly maligned by critics and the Internet. Others feel his work is juvenile at best and, at worst, incredibly self-indulgent. Most of this discussion stems from the fact that Snyder's work often adapts pre-existing material, whether it's iconic comics like Watchmen and 300 or mythology in his Netflix series Twilight of the Gods. It's Snyder's first original film, Sucker Punch , that is receiving a new lease on life , breaking into the Top 10 on HBO Max this week , per FlixPatrol. Looking at any of the trailers or stills from Sucker Punch , it's not hard to see why it's a draw for HBO Max users. The film follows Babydoll ( Emily Browning ), a young woman who is falsely institutionalized for the murder of her sister. Intending to escape before she's lobotomized, she turns to the other patients for help: Rocket ( Jena Malone ) and her sister Sweet Pea ( Abbie Cornish ), Amber ( Jamie Chung ), and "Blondie" ( Vanessa Hudgens ). The five women embark on a journey through different fantasy worlds full of stone samurai, a train full of killer robots, and steam-powered Nazi zombies. If that wasn't enough, Babydoll also fantasizes that she and her newfound friends are dancers in a brothel, which looks and sounds like a hyper-stylized and hyper-violent take on Inception. It also bears all of Snyder's signature flourishes, including slo-mo fight scenes and visuals that tend to have more definition than the characters, so what went wrong the first time around? Zack Snyder Has Yet To Realize His True Vision for ‘Sucker Punch’ When Sucker Punch had its theatrical release in 2011, it was a critical punching bag and a box office bomb. Quentin Tarantino scathingly referred to it as " one of the worst films of 2011 ", while other reviews compared it to a bad video game despite Snyder's insistence he didn't want the film to play out like one. Yet Babydoll and her friends are sent on quests to find various items, hoping to achieve a "perfect victory" that sounds more like a video game. The kicker was the fate of the main characters; nearly all the main heroines are brutally killed or maimed, which didn't earn the film any favors. Yet as time has passed, Sucker Punch has gathered a cult following and has even been examined through the lens of satire. There might be an underlying reason Sucker Punch received such a poor reception: it's not the version of the film Snyder intended to show the world. While Sucker Punch would receive a director's cut in the vein of other Snyder films , he told Empire Magazine in an interview last year that he'd like the chance to re-edit the film to match his vision : "I have the footage already shot: they just have to let me put it together. We ask every now and then. We have to ask again. I think there has to be a window when no-one’s got the movie. " Given that Snyder was eventually able to complete his version of Justice League , there's a possibility that lightning could strike twice in his favor. However, it all comes down to whether Warner Bros. Pictures is willing to pull the trigger and whether there's a similar demand for the "Snyder Cut" of Sucker Punch. Posts By Marcel Ardivan Apr 11, 2025 ‘Sucker Punch’ Was a Major Stepping Stone for One Actor Everett Collection One of the most impressive aspects of Sucker Punch , aside from its gorgeous visuals, is its stacked ensemble cast. In addition to the main heroines, Sucker Punch also features Jon Hamm , Carla Gugino , and Oscar Isaac in key roles. In the case of Isaac, he portrays Blue Jones, the main antagonist of Sucker Punch. Isaac's performance allows him to craft two different characters, as Blue's depicted as the owner of a brothel and a domineering orderly at the asylum; both are equally slimy. Isaac is often considered one of the best parts of Sucker Punch , and, thanks to that film and his appearance in Drive , 2011 was his breakout year, leading him to bigger and better performances, including Guillermo del Toro 's Frankenstein. Sucker Punch, in many ways, best defines Zack Snyder as a filmmaker. It is visually stunning and swings for the fences, but it is also extremely divisive. Now that it's made the top 10 charts on HBO Max, a whole new audience will have the chance to decide whether it's a misunderstood masterpiece or a major misfire. Murder in a Small Town - Masterpiece - Review: Tommy Cummins Makes a Return; Cassandra Gets a Message That Changes Everything Posted by Val LaRoche - November 19, 2025 0 Murder in a Small Town Reviews VL Share on Reddit There was so much going on in this episode – it’s by far one of my favorite episodes of Murder in a Small Town this season. From everything going on between Cassandra, her mother, and Mayor Holman to the return of Tommy Cummins, I was on the edge of my seat the entire episode. I was expecting more backlash from the budget vote outcome. Especially with how Karl handled hearing the news in last week’s episode. It seems like they sort of glossed over it in the beginning. I felt like this was something that really needed to be discussed. I didn’t like that Karl basically took ownership of their argument and Cassandra basically let him. Again, I understand why she was passionate about the things she wanted, but where was the empathy for Karl and the entire police department that has been running on fumes? It would’ve been nice to hear her at least apologize for the position she put him in (unless I missed it). Sid has been working doubles for over a month – running on fumes. It’s no wonder he fell asleep at the wheel and crashed his car. He was MIA the entire night and people just assumed he was sleeping in for the day. Thankfully Laila found him and he was able to get the help he needed, but man could you imagine if they never found him? "Masterpiece" - MURDER IN A SMALL TOWN, Pictured: Guest star Jamie Chung as Lanni Soo and Rossif Sutherland as Karl Alberg. Photo: Kailey Schwerman/ FOX © 2025 Fox Media LLC. All Rights Reserved. I loved the return of Tommy Cummins. Terrible - I know, but he’s one of those characters that never leaves you. His arc continues when Lanni Soo, an assistant attorney, stops by to visit Karl and inform him that his services are needed. She needs Karl’s help in convincing him to disclose the location of the rest of his victims but specifically, Beth Falconer. Tommy agreed to give the location of the rest of his victims, but will only divulge these locations to Karl. Karl knows something is off with Tommy, but Lanni has tunnel vision of getting justice for Tommy’s victims’ families. The way she was so adamant on getting this man out into the wild, I thought she was in cahoots with him. I mean she took so many risks during this transport; even quickly getting this transport approved was suspicious. I was wrong though, she was just too focused on the end goal and was unfamiliar with Tommy’s game. It’s no wonder Tommy managed to get the upperhand on them. At one of the gravesites, the box he buried his victim in was rigged with an explosive. When that went off Tommy took this opportunity to escape taking Lanni with him. "Masterpiece" - MURDER IN A SMALL TOWN, Pictured: Rossif Sutherland as Karl Alberg, guest star Noah Reid as Tommy Cummins, and guest star Patrick Roccas as Stewart. Photo: Kailey Schwerman/ FOX © 2025 Fox Media LLC. All Rights Reserved. Tommy’s prison cell depicted an incomplete painting; yes, it could be because he lost his privileges, but Karl knew better than that. Putting the incomplete pieces together, he figured out that Tommy was completing his own version of Dante’s Inferno. What was sick about Tommy is that he posed his victims into famous paintings. This man is so sick and twisted - when Karl catches up to him, he has turned this warehouse into a version of hell for anyone who enters creating a literal inferno. Multiple drum barrels up in flames except one – the one Tommy put Lanni in. Let’s take a pause for a minute to talk about this phone conversation between Cassandra and Karl. Karl calls her and the way he’s speaking, this man did not think he was making it back home to her. You can just tell he’s exhausted but giving it his all to take Tommy down. Kudos to this man Karl though, because whether or not he made it out of there alive, he set it up to make sure whatever backup came, Tommy wouldn’t make it far. "Masterpiece" - MURDER IN A SMALL TOWN, Pictured: Kristin Kreuk as Cassandra Lee. Photo: Kailey Schwerman/ FOX © 2025 Fox Media LLC. All Rights Reserved. He messed up when he didn’t take Karl out at that moment if we’re being honest (glad he didn’t). Making Karl pick between catching him or saving Lanni was a bit overconfident there, Tommy. Of course he’s captured, but returning back to the scene, you know those drum barrels on fire? Yeah, the remaining victims Tommy kept hidden. I’m glad despite the ordeal for the day, Beth Falconer’s parents and everyone else will get the closure they deserve. Do we think this is the end of Tommy Cummins? Something tells me it’s not but we shall see. The last few minutes of tonight's episode were enough to make me want the next episode yesterday. Cassandra is handed an envelope and man is her next encounter with Mayor Holman going to be an interesting one. Someone clearly hacked the mayor’s account and sent Cassandra proof of why Christie has been pushing to get this budget passed. What’d you think of tonight’s new episode of Murder in a Small Town?
