TIFFCOM rebranded its Tokyo Story Market as Tokyo IP Market: Adaptation & Remake, expanding from adaptation rights specialists to include production companies holding remake rights, with six major participants including Kadokawa, Kodansha, Square Enix, and Toei. Examples cited include China’s “Yolo” remake grossing approximately $480 million and Netflix’s live-action “One Piece” series demonstrating explosive global demand. The appetite is driven by hard numbers. Japan’s anime industry reached a record $25.3 billion in 2024, with overseas sales accounting for nearly 80% of the total market and growing at double-digit rates annually, according to figures released by the Association of Japanese Animations during TIFFCOM. The sector has doubled in size over the past decade, making Japanese content a high-stakes battleground for global studios. But attendees at The Future of Japanese Intellectual Property in Global Adaptations, a TIFFCOM keynote presentation by producer Fujimura Tetsu, came away with a different, more positive impression: For all the problems of the Japanese entertainment industry, beginning with an insular mindset that makes it slow to respond to international opportunities, it still generates IP with enormous growth potential. Founder and CEO of consulting firm Filosofia, Fujimura illustrated this thesis with not only a wealth of data and examples, but also his own story of joining hands with top Hollywood producers to bring Japanese IP to the world, from the 2017 live-action sci-fi “Ghost in the Shell” to the hit Netflix “One Piece” series. As Fujimura noted, Japanese anime has moved beyond a niche interest internationally to the global mainstream, led by the record-setting earnings of the “Demon Slayer” franchise. He also presented a long list of Japanese IP, from comics and novels to games and toys, that is now in the Hollywood content pipeline. His takeaway: Japanese IP has become a key national industry rivaling the country’s fabled automakers in earnings. Toyota may be struggling against Tesla in the global EV sweepstakes, but Hello Kitty is conquering the world. Yet despite this dominance, the emergence of world-beating IP from South Korea and China, including games, animations, movies and streaming shows, has seemingly threatened the longtime supremacy of regional pop culture powerhouse Japan. Japan’s Cultural Confidence Returns With “ Kokuho ” Leading Local Box Office Renaissance Lee Sang-il’s three-hour Kabuki period drama “Kokuho” has grossed $109 million since its June release, marking the third-highest total ever for a live-action Japanese film. The film premiered in Directors’ Fortnight at Cannes and has become a major cultural phenomenon, with government officials highlighting how it has re-inspired public interest in traditional Kabuki theater. The success reflects renewed appetite for prestige studio filmmaking reminiscent of Japan’s Golden Age auteurs, a theme that resonated throughout the festival. For example, the Production Committee style of film producing, that is common in Japan, came in for criticism, and was compared poorly to Korea’s less bureaucratic and more swashbuckling style of filmmaking, which is usually helmed by just one company. Similarly, producers complained of having to spend more money hiring bilingual crew and cast when coproducing in Japan. For example, in one platform’s presentation, none of the content demonstrated was localized into English, and video clips shown were not stripped of the extensive Japanese text overlays that are a hallmark of Japanese television, despite the platform being meant for international producers. Officials plan to use the platform to demystify Japan’s production committee financing model for overseas producers, with the goal of enabling more meaningful international co-productions, as Japan produces around 1,200 films annually with $1.31 billion in box office receipts. Despite the language barrier, Japan in general, still looms large in the imagination of Asian filmmakers. The sui generis nature of Japanese culture, practices and lifestyle continue to be a font of inspiration for directors in the region. Connie Nielsen's Eleanor of Aquitaine is my favorite character in the new MGM+ version of Robin Hood and now that episode 3 is available to stream, you can see why I'm raving about her. Acting as a mentor for Marian (Lauren McQueen), viewers learn how Eleanor manages to rule a kingdom while her husband is away and she's confined to her London-based castle. She fosters alliances through near-constant correspondence, keeping her friends close and her enemies closer. Nielsen is as captivating as she is alluring, pulling us in by being the keeper of more information than we're even aware of. Given we know Nielsen has a history of playing royalty – of course I'm talking about Lucilla, the daughter of Marcus Aurelius, in Gladiator and Gladiator II – but amazingly, her breakout role wasn't what inspired her to play the latest Queen in her roster. When I asked Nielsen what was, I would never have guessed what movie she cited as her answer... and I bet neither would you. Wonder Woman helped Connie Nielsen prepare for Robin Hood, not Gladiator Connie Nielsen as Queen of the Amazons in Wonder Woman . (Image credit: DC) "When I was, doing prep for playing the Queen of the Amazons in Wonder Woman, I was reading this incredible book by an anthropologist at Stanford," she tells me. "She pointed out in her book that female scientists had gone out and DNA tested all of these fabulous warrior graves that had been found all over Eurasia, and found that the ones that were the most famous were female. Turns out these presumptions just created prejudice." It's this kind of thinking that has so obviously informed Nielsen's approach to playing Eleanor. It's a role we've seen portrayed countless times before (most notably Katherine Hepburn in the 1968 film T he Lion of Winter ). But as you can probably guess, Nielsen didn't lean on any TV and film versions of Robin Hood . "I felt like there was so much of who she was in the writing. There was a direct line to her reality. Historians have constructed quite a lot of material for people like us to build on, so it was real pleasure to to dive into her story. He added: "I got to act for seven months, getting paid to act is unreal too. Nobody was directed by Ilya Naishuller, written by Derek Kolstad, and produced by Odenkirk himself. According to IMDB the plot is simple: "A docile family man slowly reveals his true character after his house gets burgled by two petty thieves, which, coincidentally, leads him into a bloody war with a Russian crime boss." ‌ Nobody features action sequences with Odenkirk taking on most of his own stunts as the lead actor after he underwent two years of physical training. The movie's story was also said to be partly inspired by Odenkirk's own experiences with home invasions, though he has stated the traumatic ones were not the primary motivation behind the intense storyline. ‌ For film fans looking for an action packed watch, Nobody appears to tick the boxes with viewers full of praise for Odenkirk in the leading role. Filled with witty and high paced action sequences, many film fans have said it's perfect for those that love films like John Wick. View 3 Images Gladiator star Connie Nielsen (left) stars as Odenkirk's on-screen wife in Nobody (Image: YouTube/Universal Pictures) Writing on Rotten Tomatoes, one review gave the film five stars with a simple review: "This movie is good because its like a more mild version of john wick.' ‌ Another five star review wrote: "Very entertaining. I’m a huge John wick fan and I loved how this had its own flair and cause. Made me want to watch the second one right after. I always enjoy getting to watch Bob Odenkirk. And this was such a very fun movie. We laughed out loud several times. It was extremely enjoyable. If you enjoy action movies at all, you must watch this. Christopher Lloyd really looked like he was genuinely enjoying himself," said another with five stars. Others claimed the film was 'worth every penny', as one person wrote: "I finally watched it.. This action movie is a smash. Worth every penny." View 3 Images Fans of John Wick are urged to watch Nobody as another action packed favourite (Image: Lionsgate) ‌ Another begged for film fans to see it, as they posted" '"Excellent movie! I have watched it over and over again, and have loved it everytime. Must see movie for action fans!" Film fans also got a second hit with a sequel, Nobody 2, released in the summer picking up where the other film ended. The sequel has also earned five star reviews and praise from movie fans as many claim they've been 'binge watching' the two together. Directed by Timo Tjahjanto. Starring Bob Odenkirk, Connie Nielsen, Christopher Lloyd, John Ortiz, RZA, Sharon Stone, Colin Salmon, Colin Hanks, Gage Munroe, and Paisley Cadorath. SYNOPSIS: A former assassin-turned-suburban-family-man takes his family on a holiday to get away from his violent ways, but circumstances won’t let him rest. 2021s Nobody was something of a sleeper hit, bouncing off the back of the John Wick movies with some of the same crew involved, and giving middle-aged dads everywhere a bit of hope as all-round-nice-guy Hutch Mansell (Bob Odenkirk) had enough of being taken for granted by his family, neighbours and colleagues, and his secret former life as a special ops assassin came racing back to the surface, resulting in him burning $30 million dollars of a Russian gangster’s money. And so now we have the inevitable follow-up where, in true sequel tradition, things get ramped up and are even more violent and action-packed than before. We catch up with Hutch, who is paying back the Russian money by doing covert missions for ‘The Barber’ (Colin Salmon), but eliminating dozens of bad guys when you’re a middle-aged man takes its toll, and with his marriage to wife Becca (Connie Nielsen) and relationship with teenage son Brady (Gage Munroe) feeling the strain of him not being there when he is needed, Hutch decides to take the family – including young daughter Sammy (Paisley Cadorath) and grandfather David (Christopher Lloyd) – on vacation to a small-town theme park to unwind. However, trouble is never far away and once Hutch loses his cool with the park’s security, a chain of events puts him and his family in the sights of corrupt Sheriff Abel (Colin Hanks) and local crime boss Lendina (Sharon Stone). Most franchises take until the third movie until they nail down the formula, as part two’s nearly always try something different before reverting to what made the original so popular for the next movie, but Nobody 2 dispenses with any notions of experimenting and gets right down to the action, which is a little bloodier and – and it sounds a bit silly to say it for a movie that revels in violence – a bit more mean-spirited than before. Yes, shooting nameless bad guys from a distance in a geyser of blood squibs is fun, but slamming a man’s head into a bench saw feels a tad more personal. To be fair, the camera does cut away from actually seeing his head get split open, but it still adds a modicum of grindhouse brutality to an otherwise slick studio action thriller. The bulk of the original cast return but having Christopher Lloyd and not using him for anything other than the odd quip feels like a waste, especially when he was such a highlight of the first movie. John Ortiz shows up as the owner of the theme park and adds some extra energy, and Sharon Stone clearly revels in playing Lendina, the ruthless crime boss who wipes out whole bloodlines if she gets ripped off, but Colin Hanks looks a little bewildered playing the corrupt sheriff in Lendina’s pocket. He talks tough, but is never really convincing, especially as he doesn’t get to kill anyone, which might have lent some weight to his character. But overall, Nobody 2 carries on Hutch Mansell’s story without mixing up the formula too much. The violence is superbly choreographed and shot in a similar way, albeit it with a few more slow-motion pieces for intensity, and those set pieces do look excellent in 4K UHD, with the slow-motion showing off a lot of detail and the quick edits crisp and clean. When combined with the punchy Dolby Atmos track the action gets really elevated, so if you have the setup then this is the format to watch it on. We also get a few more character beats we didn’t have before – who knew that Becca was such a good shot in the fun fair shooting range? Maybe that will come in handy at some point – but as the plot is paper thin and basically does the first movie again nothing is expanded upon to any great degree. Overall, though, if you liked Nobody then you’ll like Nobody 2 , but probably not quite as much. Picture by Binge FILM CLUB Binge There's nothing like a heartfelt British dramedy to lift your spirits. Black Friday Offers Subscribe today for the news that matters Login or signup to continue reading All articles from our website & app The digital version of Today's Paper Crosswords, Sudoku and Trivia All other regional websites in your area Continue Film Club is a charming, sweet and not-too-sappy six-episode adventure tailor-made for cinephiles. Co-created by star Aimee Lou Wood (who was so impressive in The White Lotus ), the extremely bingeable series follows best buds Evie (Wood) and Noa (Nabhaan Rizwan, Kaos ) as they gather every Friday to watch a movie in Evie's garage. But watch is not all they do - they go all out. The garage is transformed to match the world of whichever film they're watching, and they must also dress up as one of the characters - the more obscure the better (for instance, when they watch The Shawshank Redemption , Evie dresses as Jake, the crow Brooks befriends). The viewing is followed by trivia and great fun is had by all. It doesn't take long to work out that this charming weekly activity is less of a hobby and more of a crutch for our two leads. Evie hasn't been able to leave the house for eight months, constrained by some fear in her brain that she can't quite figure out. Noa is anxious about taking steps in his career and his life, and their film club gives him a convenient reason not to make any changes. Wood and Rizwan are both brilliant and incredibly likeable leads, and they are well supported by Suranne Jones ( The Assassin ), Adam Long ( Nine Bodies in a Mexican Morgue ), Liv Hill ( The Serpent Queen ), Fola Evans-Akingbola ( The Night Agent ) and Adolescence breakout Owen Cooper. The quiet but simmering romantic tension between Evie and Noa is excellent to watch unfold and the pair have an easy chemistry. As much, if not more, about family love as it is about romance, Film Club is one of the unexpected joys of the year. Damian Hardung and Harriet Herbig-Matten in Maxton Hall: The World Between Us. Picture by Prime Video MAXTON HALL: THE WORLD BETWEEN US Prime Video After a buzzy and successful first season, German high school series Maxton Hall makes its return for an even more drama-filled season two. Our leads Ruby (Harriet Herbig-Matten) and James (Damian Hardung) ended their first season in a happy place, relationship-wise, but that's thrown into turmoil immediately as James learns of the unexpected death of his mother and goes on a self-destructive spiral. In true Maxton Hall style, Ruby's educational prospects somehow rest on whether or not she and the school's student events team can pull together various successful fundraisers and dinners for the cohort and their rich and influential parents. While the believability of just about everything in this show is thin at best, it does make for fun and engaging drama, especially when paired with the incredibly liberal use of slow-motion cinematography and off-kilter camera angles. This season also continues Lydia's struggle to be taken seriously by her and James' insufferably villainous father, as well as her little bun in the oven situation. But like any high school romance show, Maxton Hall lives and dies by its leads' chemistry, and Herbig-Matten and Hardung have it through the roof. Existing fans will love this season as much as the first, and won't be able to wait for season three. Ruth Wilson and Emma Thompson in Down Cemetery Road. Picture by AppleTV+ DOWN CEMETERY ROAD AppleTV+ Pair Ruth Wilson and Emma Thompson together and you'll give anything a go, even if it's terrible. Luckily for us, Down Cemetery Road is far from terrible. The British series, which has episodes dropping weekly, introduces us to Oxfordshire-based classic art restorer Sarah (Wilson) who becomes obsessed with finding a child injured in a house explosion neighbouring her property. Her fixation starts innocently enough, as she is simply trying to pass along a handmade 'get well soon' card to the kid from one of the other children in the neighbourhood. But she's stopped at the hospital and asked to leave. Then she finds press coverage of the explosion has edited the child out of the narrative. Her final straw is when police say information on the injured girl has been flagged and cannot be shared. So she hires a private investigator to look into the perplexing situation, driven by a need to know what's going on. That puts her on contact with Thompson's no-nonsense Zoe. She's capable, witty and not one for keeping with tradition. And as with any Thompson character, you can't help but like her immediately. The series is from the creator of the celebrated Slow Horses , and looks set to be an engaging, enjoyable mystery with a good deal of humour and quirks to complement the intrigue and darkness. ALSO STREAMING Connie Nielsen and Sean Bean in Robin Hood. Picture by Stan The famed archer of Nottingham is back for another iteration with Stan's new modernised retelling of Robin Hood . The period series stars Sean Bean and Connie Nielsen. There's plenty of new content on Netflix, with Colin Farrell poker drama Ballad of a Small Player; Aussie Superwog spin-off series Son of a Donkey ; the return of fantasy series The Witcher , now with Aussie Liam Hemsworth taking over the Geralt role from Henry Cavill; and Aileen: Queen of the Serial Killers , a documentary film about Aileen Wuornos, who was portrayed by Charlize Theron in the Oscar-winning film Monster . Over on Paramount+ Tracy Morgan leads new sitcom Crutch , a spin-off from The Neighbourhood . And on Prime Video you'll find Hedda , writer-director Nia DaCosta's new take on the classic Henrik Ibsen play Hedda Gabler, with Tessa Thompson in the lead. MGM+ By Rachel Holbrook Published Nov 3, 2025 Rachel Holbrook has been writing about pop culture and entertainment for over five years online, after developing a borderline unhealthy obsession with Tinseltown at a young age. A self-proclaimed Hollywood connoisseur, Rachel is a huge fan of the Golden Age of Cinema and is thrilled she gets paid to talk about her passions. Hollywood has had success bringing the folk hero to life on both the big and small screens , with famous faces like Errol Flynn, Kevin Costner, and Russell Crowe among the leading men who have tackled the iconic character. Now, newcomer Jack Patten is looking to leave his mark on the bandit and headline the MGM+ series Robin Hood . The adventure series chronicles the epic romance between Robin Hood and Marian, following their quest to bring peace to England, and stars Sean Bean, Lauren McQueen, and Connie Nielsen. It's debuting on November 2, 2025, on MGM+. The reimagining will consist of 10 exciting episodes that will provide audiences with endless entertainment throughout the holidays, with the season finale slated to air on December 28, 202 5. Let's take a look at the release schedule for Robin Hood. How Many Episodes Will Be in 'Robin Hood'? MGM+ MGM+'s thrilling reimagining of the Robin Hood tale is set to make its highly anticipated debut on Sunday, November 2, 2025, at 9/8c p.m. , with two episodes of the series dropping on its premiere day. New installments will subsequently be released weekly on Sundays, and the season will include a total of 10 episodes, concluding its run on December 28, 2025. So far, only two episode titles have been officially disclosed, with "I See Him" and "A Heinous Devil" both slated to debut on November 2, exclusively on MGM+. The legendary outlaw of Sherwood Forest is back and ready to embark upon another thrilling adventure in the MGM+ original series Robin Hood , which features newcomer Jack Patten as the heroic bandit Robin "Rob" Hood . He, along with his band of Merry Men, fights for freedom against oppressive forces. Hollywood veteran Sean Bean stars as Rob's tyrannical, tax-loving archenemy, the Sheriff of Nottingham, whose overwhelming greed and quick temper make him an immediate adversary of the iconic figure. Bean has appeared in a slew of hit TV shows and films throughout his enduring career, including Game of Thrones , The Lord of the Rings trilogy, and Time. Determined to bring peace to England following the Norman invasion, Rob is assisted in his epic quest by Marian (Lauren McQueen) . The sharp, highly courageous young woman infiltrates the Norman courts to combat royal corruption and fight on Rob's behalf. McQueen had previously appeared in shows like Hollyoaks and Masters of the Air, as well as in Robert Zemeckis' Here . Supporting cast members include Connie Nielsen as Eleanor of Aquitaine, Marcus Fraser as Rob's trusted sidekick Little John, and Lydia Peckham as Priscilla of Nottingham. The official logline for Robin Hood reads: "A Saxon forester's son, Rob, and the daughter of a Norman lord, Marian, work together to fight for justice and freedom following the Norman invasion of England in the Middle Ages. Rob becomes the leader of a band of rebel outlaws while Marian infiltrates the Norman courts, as they collaborate to thwart royal corruption and bring peace to England." Who Is the Creative Team Behind 'Robin Hood'? Robin Hood & his Merry Men in Robin Hood MGM+ Showrunner John Glenn co-wrote the screenplay for Robin Hood alongside fellow episode director Jonathan English, having worked on scripts for movies like Eagle Eye and The Lazarus Project, and having produced and written for shows including SEAL Team and Hatfields & McCoys . English also has extensive experience in both TV and film, with credits including The Librarians: The Next Chapter and The Outpost . Joining the duo as an executive producer is Todd Lieberman, who earned an Oscar nomination for his work on The Fighter and has also produced Warm Bodies and Beauty and the Beast. Promising to bring a "modern energy" and depict the blossoming love story between Rob and Marian in a show billed as a "sweeping, romantic adventure," Robin Hood is looking to tell an authentic yet refreshing retelling of the classic tale , with the head of MGM+, Michael Wright , calling the series "the epitome of our brand promise" before further saying: "This is a new imagining of the classic tale of the roguish outlaw hero who stole from the rich and gave to the poor. It’s an exciting, smart, sweeping, romantic adventure that brings historical authenticity, psychological depth, and a heightened focus on the relationship between Rob and Marian to the beloved story." (dpa) New TV series "Robin Hood" explores the legendary outlaw's origins with a personal take and previously unseen historical authenticity, the show's creators say. The latest reimagining tells the tale of how Robin Hood came to be the medieval English folk hero who robbed the rich to feed the poor. Known simply as "Rob", it sees the Saxon forester's son and skilled archer transform into a rebel after experiencing devastating losses and injustices. Australian newcomer Jack Patten follows in the footsteps of several Hollywood stars to portray the hero of Sherwood Forest. But while Patten found his first lead role somewhat daunting, the 28-year-old did not feel weighed down by previous interpretations - he had not seen any of them. "It's a weird thing, because I feel like a lot of people have heard of Robin Hood. I was one of those people. I'd heard of Robin Hood, but I'd never seen it," Patten said at the show's London premiere on Tuesday. "Every generation deserves a Robin Hood, and the fact that we get to be this gen's Robin Hood is pretty awesome," he said. The 10-episode first season is set in 12th century post-Norman invasion England and also centers on Rob's love story with Marian (Lauren McQueen), the daughter of a Norman lord, who has taken over the ancestral home of Rob's ousted Saxon family. The series is brought to the screen by co-creators John Glenn and Jonathan English, who set out to offer a modern and more intimate depiction of the events and the time period. "It was the idea of doing an origin story, which we've never really seen before, how Robin becomes an outlaw, what happens to him, what happens to his parents," said English. "It's about the Norman conquest of England. It's about class. We've never really seen a Robin Hood story that's really about class, but it is. Robin, from the rich giving to the poor is in itself about class. So I think it's very topical, very relevant today," he said. The show's ensemble cast also features actors Sean Bean as the Sheriff of Nottingham and Connie Nielsen in the role of Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine. "Robin Hood" starts streaming on MGM+ on November 2. (Reuters) A new episode of the "Beatles Anthology", 30 years after the original landmark series, shows the impact on Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr of being in the biggest rock band in history, its writer and director said. The original eight-part documentary, broadcast in 1995, spanned the band's gritty early days in Liverpool and Hamburg to the phenomenon of Beatlemania and global superstardom and the break-up in 1970. The "Anthology" project included the single "Free as a Bird", created in the 1990s from a demo recorded by John Lennon in 1977, three years before he was murdered. The remastered series, with a ninth episode including unseen 1990s footage of McCartney, Harrison and Starr, debuts on Disney+ on Wednesday. "The new episode is untethered from the chronology of the original episodes," writer and director Oliver Murray said. "One to eight is the literal birth of the Beatles through to their break-up in 1970, and episode nine is able to speak to the inward-looking sense of what it was like to be a Beatle." The film was restored by an Apple Corps production team working with Peter Jackson's Park Road Post company in New Zealand, with technology Jackson used to make "The Beatles: Get Back" documentary, which premiered in 2021. "The whole of the Beatles archive has been restored and is now digital," Murray said. "Every time we went into the edit suite it was almost like stepping back in time to the mid-90s." He said Jackson's documentary changed the mythology of the Beatles, which until then had been etched in stone. "What 'Get Back' did was break down those stereotypes, and we see them more as very young men," he said. The new episode gives fans an opportunity to learn about the band from scratch, with an understanding of who they were as people, he said. "The reason that the Beatles story still resonates is because it's 20th-century folklore," he said. (Reuters) A new episode of the "Beatles Anthology", 30 years after the original landmark series, shows the impact on Paul McCartney, George Harrison and Ringo Starr of being in the biggest rock band in history, its writer and director said. The original eight-part documentary, broadcast in 1995, spanned the band's gritty early days in Liverpool and Hamburg to the phenomenon of Beatlemania and global superstardom and the break-up in 1970. The "Anthology" project included the single "Free as a Bird", created in the 1990s from a demo recorded by John Lennon in 1977, three years before he was murdered. The remastered series, with a ninth episode including unseen 1990s footage of McCartney, Harrison and Starr, debuts on Disney+ on Wednesday. "The new episode is untethered from the chronology of the original episodes," writer and director Oliver Murray said. "One to eight is the literal birth of the Beatles through to their break-up in 1970, and episode nine is able to speak to the inward-looking sense of what it was like to be a Beatle. " The film was restored by an Apple Corps production team working with Peter Jackson's Park Road Post company in New Zealand, with technology Jackson used to make "The Beatles: Get Back" documentary, which premiered in 2021. "The whole of the Beatles archive has been restored and is now digital," Murray said. "Every time we went into the edit suite it was almost like stepping back in time to the mid-90s. " He said Jackson's documentary changed the mythology of the Beatles, which until then had been etched in stone. "What 'Get Back' did was break down those stereotypes, and we see them more as very young men," he said. The new episode gives fans an opportunity to learn about the band from scratch, with an understanding of who they were as people, he said. "The reason that the Beatles story still resonates is because it's 20th-century folklore," he said. "It is a timeless story of some lads from Liverpool who share a dream and go on to conquer the world. Comments What's On Hayley Anderson TV Reporter 08:30, 22 Nov 2025 A legend from Breaking Bad is set to grace our television screens tonight in an "extremely bloody" action film . ‌ The 2021 movie Nobody follows the life of Hutch Mansell (portrayed by Bob Odenkirk ) as it spirals into chaos when burglars invade his home and he decides to take justice into his own hands. ‌ However, his actions provoke a crime boss after Hutch assaults his brother, leading him to fight for his life against dangerous consequences. ‌ At the centre of Nobody is none other than Breaking Bad' s icon Bob Odenkirk, who played Saul Goodman throughout all five series before landing his own spin-off Better Call Saul for six seasons. Viewers will have the chance to see Odenkirk in a completely different role in Nobody tonight, Saturday, November 22, at 9pm on Film4. (Image: EIGHTY TWO FILMS) ‌ Odenkirk isn't the only recognisable face in Nobody, as he is joined by Gladiator and Wonder Woman actress Connie Nielsen, who plays Hutch's disappointed wife Becca. Additionally, the unforgettable star of Back to the Future, Christopher Lloyd, portrays Hutch's father David Mansell. Since its release, fans have been sharing their opinions of the film on review aggregator Rotten Tomatoes, with many drawing comparisons to the classic action film franchise John Wick. ‌ "Nobody" is better than the first John Wick", one viewer claimed, while another agreed: "Fans of the John Wick series and anyone stuck in a career rut will enjoy this ludicrously plotted revenge. View 2 Images The 2021 film Nobody stars Bob Odenkirk and Christopher Lloyd. (Image: EIGHTY TWO FILMS) " One viewer praised: "Nobody is an arresting action showcase for star Bob Odenkirk and a skillfully staged spectacle of stuntwork nearly on par with the John Wick trilogy. ‌ "Another fan couldn't help but compliment Odenkirk's "unsurprisingly brilliant" acting, stating: "A unique take on the action genre, Nobody is lean, mean, and showcases a delightful Odenkirk leading the way through all the carnage. "Odenkirk submits his action hero punch card and can take my money any day of the week with it all", chimed in another enthusiast." "A real winner! Great film. Must see!" insisted another viewer, while a fellow commenter added: "Odenkirk is a delight, as he is in everything he does. " Article continues below Nobody is available on Saturday, November 22, at 9pm on Film4. text: Robin Hood review: Sean Bean is brilliant but this newcomer steals the spotlight - The Mirror ‌ ‌ Skip to main content News Celebs Football Lifestyle More InYourArea Funeral Notices Shop Competitions Dating Offers Newsletter Signup Follow us on social Daily Mirror Icon TV TV News Robin Hood Robin Hood review: Sean Bean is brilliant but this newcomer steals the spotlight The 2025 adaptation of Robin Hood starring Sean Bean is in a league of its own. Comments TV Katie Palmer 09:56, 03 Nov 2025 Updated 13:18, 03 Nov 2025 Robin Hood has started airing weekly on MGM+ and the latest adaptation tells the title character's story from a new perspective. ‌ Set in the early days before Rob of Loxley secured his infamous moniker, the series tells of his devastating losses and complex love stories. ‌ While the Robin Hood series stars some household names, like Sean Bean as the Sheriff of Nottingham and Connie Nielsen as Eleanor of Aquitaine, it is newcomer Jack Patten who steals the show alongside his co-star Lauren McQueen as Marian. ‌ The title character is Australian actor Jack Patten's first major TV role, with the star having only previously appeared in an episode of NCIS: Sydney. Yet his performance in the MGM+ series would suggest he has a decades-long list of credits behind him. READ MORE : Robin Hood star shares honest thoughts on working with Sean Bean READ MORE : Where was Sean Bean's Robin Hood series filmed? View 2 Images Sean Bean stars in Robin Hood (Image: MGM+) ‌ Despite only graduating from the National Institute of Dramatic Arts in Sydney in 2023, his dedication to the role is unparalleled. Performing a large number of his own stunts, his commitment to bringing out the best in such an iconic character has been noted. On a separate note, his co-star Lauren McQueen shines equally as bright as Maid Marian, as the character's harrowing backstory and family history is explored in more detail. ‌ The pair's chemistry is undeniable, and they are utterly convincing as tortured lovers, ripped apart by family politics. An emotionally challenging role, McQueen masterfully captures how Marian is torn between her family and her own heart as she contends with her vicious father, the Earl of Huntingdon (Steven Waddington). View 2 Images Lauren McQueen plays Maid Marian ‌ Sean Bean naturally captivates all in his complex role as the sheriff - a refreshing change from other adaptations which portray the character as the archenemy. Yet he is by no means the standout star of the show, with many contenders standing out, including Angus Castle-Doughty as Friar Tuck. As for the pace of the series, the adventure is easy to follow, with 10 episodes airing weekly until the finale on December 28. ‌ Each episode has equal measures of action and drama, and not a single moment has been wasted. The series is worthy of a primetime linear TV slot. There has been no word on the show's future, but it is off to a promising start. Lured by the brilliance of Middle Earth from an early age both in print and on screen, his palate has since expanded to other realms including Westeros , Kattegat among others. Sign in to your Collider account follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Not many people showed up to see Bob Odenkirk ’s latest action sequel in theaters, but months later, the Breaking Bad star is getting the last laugh. Nobody 2 has become a surprise smash hit on streaming, dominating PVOD charts across several countries, including the U.S. As of this writing, the action thriller ranks as the most-demanded title on Amazon among American audiences and the fifth most popular movie on iTunes. It’s an impressive turnaround for a film that struggled at the summer box office and was written off as a commercial flop. The sequel brings Odenkirk back as Hutch Mansell, the unassuming family man with a deadly past. This time, Hutch attempts to step away from his life as an assassin for some much-needed family time. But chaos inevitably trails him to his vacation spot in Plummerville, which just happens to sit along a bootlegging route run by ruthless crime boss, Lendina ( Sharon Stone ). Despite earning a generally positive critical reception, Nobody 2 struggled to connect with moviegoers and failed to break even at the box office. Produced on a $25 million budget, the film ended its theatrical run with a global gross of $41 million , falling short of its predecessor’s strong post-pandemic performance, which earned more than three times its production cost. It now seems audiences have developed a newfound appreciation for the sequel, directed by action maestro Timo Tjahjanto . Since becoming available on PVOD in October, Nobody 2 has been a smash success . From Europe to Asia, Australia, the United Kingdom, and even Africa, the film is finally getting its due, drawing attention from viewers worldwide to rank high on several PVOD platforms. Audience reception on Rotten Tomatoes has remained solid, with the movie now holding a verified 88% score on the Popcorn Meter from over a thousand reviews , standing well above its 77% critical rating. Will There Be More 'Nobody' Films? There hasn’t been any recent update on the franchise’s future, but Odenkirk previously revealed that the original plan was to expand Nobody into a three- or four-film series . Those ambitions initially seemed jeopardized by the sequel’s underwhelming box office run. However, its recent success on PVOD might just be enough to get Universal to sign on for another adventure. Those who have tuned in for the new MGM+ production from Jonathan English and John Glenn will know that the creative pair have cracked the code and done exactly that. Already three episodes in, the title is climbing the streaming charts and winning over critics and audiences alike. Today, we’re thrilled to share an exclusive sneak peek of the upcoming fourth episode of the fantasy series, which features a masterclass in acting from Gladiator and Nobody favorite, Connie Nielsen , and Hollyoaks alum, Lauren McQueen . Our exclusive first look at Robin Hood ’s fourth episode takes viewers inside the chambers of Nielsen’s Queen Eleanor , where she’s called Marian (McQueen) for a meeting. From behind her desk, the Queen lists her royal titles before telling Marian that even with all the names and jobs in the world, she’s still considered by many to be a prisoner of England. But, she explains, there is still power in her position, as she is able to exchange messages with others and “make allegiances” with the right people, all while ruling from the background. Further driving her point home, the Queen tells Marian that she, too, can harness her power with a little help from the most powerful woman in the castle — the Queen. Starring Jack Patten ( War Machine ) as Rob, Robin Hood weaves a different tale than what audiences are used to while keeping the main plot points in place. This one is a story of love between the titular character and Marian (McQueen), both of whom couldn’t be more different. The former is the son of a Saxon forester, and the latter is the daughter of a Norman lord, but that doesn’t stop their paths from crossing and a romantic and professional relationship beginning. From outside the castle walls, Rob assembles a gang of outlaws intent on bringing the royals to their knees, while Marian uses her power and connections to do the same inside the courts. Meet the Faces Behind ‘Robin Hood’ Robin Hood sees the return of Sean Bean into the fantasy world following his less-than-savory send-offs in The Lord of the Rings and Game of Thrones . The legendary actor is joined by a cast that includes Lydia Peckham ( Nuremberg ), Henry Rowley , Angus Castle-Doughty ( Showtrial ), Marcus Fraser ( The Last Knight ), Steve Waddington ( The Last of the Mohicans ), and others. Universal Pictures Nobody 2 — the sequel to Bob Odenkirk’s hit 2021 crime comedy Nobody — is coming soon to streaming on Peacock. Nobody 2 opened in theaters on Aug. 15 before its debut on digital streaming via premium video on demand on Sept. 2. Set four years after the first film. Odenkirk ( Better Call Saul , Breaking Bad ) reprises his role as Hutch Mansell in Nobody 2 . In the 2021 film, Hutch, a former assassin for the CIA, took on the Russian mob and burned $30 million of the underworld organization’s cash. Forbes Will There Be A ‘Chad Powers’ Season 2? Here’s Some Encouraging News By Tim Lammers In Nobody 2 , Hutch is now indebted to another criminal heavy and he must pay the Russian’s money by performing an endless series of mob hits — but he’s in serious need of a break. According to an announcement by Peacock on Tuesday, Nobody 2 will make its streaming video on demand debut on the NBC Universal streaming platform on Friday, Nov. 14. Peacock offers two streaming plans. The ad-based Peacock Premium tier is available for $10.99 per month or $109.99 per year, while an ad-free Peacock Premium Plus tier costs $16.99 per month or $169.99 per year. Debuting on MGM+ in early November, this reimagined version of Robin Hood, created by John Glenn, offers a deeper exploration of its characters. It particularly focuses on the relationship between Rob (Patten) and Marian (Lauren McQueen) as they work together to quell royal corruption. With a Robin Hood cast that includes Sean Bean as the Sheriff of Nottingham, Lydia Peckham as Priscilla of Nottingham, Steven Waddington as the Earl of Huntingdon, and Connie Nielsen as Queen Eleanor of Aquitaine, the ten-episode adventure drama has garnered a generally positive reception. It currently sits at 73% on Rotten Tomatoes, with the audience score rising to 80%. In an interview with The Manchester Evening News , Patten enthusiastically addressed the possibility of season 2. The actor says he would love to return, sharing that it would be exciting. He also praises John Glenn and director Jonathan English for creating rich, engaging characters. In the quote below, Patten also shares that there's plenty of material for another batch of episodes: “We would love to do a [season] 2. That would be awesome. Jonathan [English] and John [Glenn] just wrote awesome characters. As actors we love an arc, you can't ask for much more.” McQueen echoes Patten's enthusiasm, saying she would “ definitely ” come back if the show is renewed. She previews that the season finale ends in an exciting place for each character, offering opportunities for the world to evolve. McQueen also highlights the working atmosphere, praising the young performers that she works with and noting how the positive atmosphere on-set translates to the screen: “I think the season ends quite interestingly for every single character. I think it could develop, but we just wanted to do the best we could for season 1. It's a really exciting young cast as well, so talented. I'm so excited for everyone to see new actors. We were just like a big family at the end and I think you can really see that energy on screen.” There are no public viewership numbers for Robin Hood . However, looking at third-party data, such as the streaming tracker FlixPatrol , the adventure drama has been at the top of the charts in both the U.S. and the U.K. since November 13. Considering that MGM+ is a smaller streamer with fewer originals, that could be a point in its favor. Also, when considering a renewal, it helps to look at the trajectory of other MGM+ originals, such as From season 4 . To take the example of a Stephen King adaptation series, which similarly caught on with viewers, The Institute season 1 finale aired before the renewal announcement. If it's the case that Robin Hood follows along the lines of other breakout MGM+ dramas, the reimagined series could get the thumbs up before its finale debuts on December 28. That's still a little while away. Got it Normal text size Larger text size Very large text size There’s almost an unspoken rule that actors playing beloved characters – say, a superhero or a plastic doll – have to stress how central that figure’s been throughout their life. But Australian Jack Patten, the latest actor in a long line to take on folklore vigilante Robin Hood , holds no such pretences. “When I thought of Robin Hood, I thought about the fox – even though I never watched that cartoon version ,” he says, sitting at a cafe in Sydney, opposite Kings Cross Fountain. “I didn’t grow up watching Robin Hood, but I did know of him.” Perhaps the honest answer is because Patten’s new to this. The glossy 10-part TV series acts as the 28-year-old actor’s introduction to the world, going head-to-head with action hero Sean Bean two years after graduating from the National Institute of Dramatic Arts (NIDA). Jack Patten stars as the titular Robin Hood in this upcoming series. Credit: Aleksandar Letic/MGM+ Far more mature than Disney’s animated fox, 2025’s Robin Hood is a decidedly post -Game of Thrones historical drama, not shy of sordid scenes or blood spills. Made for MGM+, the US streamer behind period dramas such as Billy the Kid , the series (airing on Stan* in Australia) is a gripping drama for fans of classic stories told well and with a prestige TV budget. It’s Hollywood’s first take on the folk legend since 2018’s box-office failure starring Taron Egerton , and arrives ahead of A24’s film The Death of Robin Hood , starring Hugh Jackman, due next year. “I think that theme of justice is forever going to be something that audiences are attracted to,” says Patten, when asked why we keep coming back to Robin Hood. “It’s timeless.” Advertisement Loading Tracing the origins of the long-standing English folk hero, Patten is a more grounded Rob, a soon-to-be teenage orphan surviving in the dark-and-gritty Middle Ages. In his grief, he rises up against Norman conquerors who have stolen his pagan community’s land and outlawed their religion. “It felt really human, despite it being quite genre, being set in the 1100s, with romance and swords and all that stuff,” he says. “That’s what really perks my ears.” Wrangling a band of outlaws and with help from Norman love-interest Marian (Lauren McQueen, Masters of the Air ) who acts as a spy, Rob bends his bow towards justice – and against the corrupt Sheriff of Nottingham, played by the imposing, steely Bean. The cast has a few more familiar faces, such as Connie Nielsen ( Gladiator ) and Steven Waddington ( The Last of the Mohicans ), but is filled with newcomers, which kept the eight-month shoot in Serbia energetic, even at -7°C. Connie Nielsen and Sean Bean as Eleanor of Aquitaine and the Sheriff of Nottingham in Robin Hood. Credit: Aleksandar Letic/MGM+ As far as debut roles go, a classic hero with a heart of gold is a potential star-making turn – and “a pretty awesome Christmas present”, as Patten landed the role last December. Advertisement “I was speechless,” he says. “And then I went over to Serbia in mid-January to get the bow and arrow under my belt and learn how to ride a horse. There were a few boxes to tick.” Patten loved that three-week training intensive, a process reminiscent of his time in the Sydney Swans Academy as a teen, working towards his childhood dream of being a professional AFL player. [This] stuff used to be really wanky to me ... we spoke differently at footy Jack Patten Raised by a single mum in Western Sydney’s Hills District, Patten obsessed over footy, first from afar – his mum wouldn’t let him play until he was 13 – before later landing a spot in the Academy. In 2017, a knee injury finished a superstar career before it started. At least, that’s how it felt at the time. Nearly a decade later, Patten sees it a little differently. “I loved footy. Loved watching it. Loved playing it,” he says. “Ultimately though, I wasn’t good enough. Okay, I had injuries, but I just wasn’t there. I don’t know whether that was a pill that I couldn’t swallow, if it was in my subconscious a little bit.” Jack Patten was ‘speechless’ when he was offered the role of Robin Hood last year. Credit: Janie Barrett Spending the next few years working at a school, slightly adrift, it was a colleague who first suggested acting classes in Chippendale. But his first class at The Hub Studio, run by veteran teacher Kevin Jackson, featured no acting at all. Picture by Binge FILM CLUB Binge There's nothing like a heartfelt British dramedy to lift your spirits. Subscribe now for unlimited access. Login or signup to continue reading Supporter Subscription Unlimited access on the web Breaking news alerts direct to your inbox The digital version of Today's Paper Crosswords, Sudoku and Trivia Supporting local news Continue Film Club is a charming, sweet and not-too-sappy six-episode adventure tailor-made for cinephiles. Co-created by star Aimee Lou Wood (who was so impressive in The White Lotus ), the extremely bingeable series follows best buds Evie (Wood) and Noa (Nabhaan Rizwan, Kaos ) as they gather every Friday to watch a movie in Evie's garage. But watch is not all they do - they go all out. The garage is transformed to match the world of whichever film they're watching, and they must also dress up as one of the characters - the more obscure the better (for instance, when they watch The Shawshank Redemption , Evie dresses as Jake, the crow Brooks befriends). The viewing is followed by trivia and great fun is had by all. It doesn't take long to work out that this charming weekly activity is less of a hobby and more of a crutch for our two leads. Evie hasn't been able to leave the house for eight months, constrained by some fear in her brain that she can't quite figure out. Noa is anxious about taking steps in his career and his life, and their film club gives him a convenient reason not to make any changes. Wood and Rizwan are both brilliant and incredibly likeable leads, and they are well supported by Suranne Jones ( The Assassin ), Adam Long ( Nine Bodies in a Mexican Morgue ), Liv Hill ( The Serpent Queen ), Fola Evans-Akingbola ( The Night Agent ) and Adolescence breakout Owen Cooper. The quiet but simmering romantic tension between Evie and Noa is excellent to watch unfold and the pair have an easy chemistry. As much, if not more, about family love as it is about romance, Film Club is one of the unexpected joys of the year. Damian Hardung and Harriet Herbig-Matten in Maxton Hall: The World Between Us. Picture by Prime Video MAXTON HALL: THE WORLD BETWEEN US Prime Video After a buzzy and successful first season, German high school series Maxton Hall makes its return for an even more drama-filled season two. Our leads Ruby (Harriet Herbig-Matten) and James (Damian Hardung) ended their first season in a happy place, relationship-wise, but that's thrown into turmoil immediately as James learns of the unexpected death of his mother and goes on a self-destructive spiral. In true Maxton Hall style, Ruby's educational prospects somehow rest on whether or not she and the school's student events team can pull together various successful fundraisers and dinners for the cohort and their rich and influential parents. While the believability of just about everything in this show is thin at best, it does make for fun and engaging drama, especially when paired with the incredibly liberal use of slow-motion cinematography and off-kilter camera angles. This season also continues Lydia's struggle to be taken seriously by her and James' insufferably villainous father, as well as her little bun in the oven situation. But like any high school romance show, Maxton Hall lives and dies by its leads' chemistry, and Herbig-Matten and Hardung have it through the roof. Existing fans will love this season as much as the first, and won't be able to wait for season three. Ruth Wilson and Emma Thompson in Down Cemetery Road. Picture by AppleTV+ DOWN CEMETERY ROAD AppleTV+ Pair Ruth Wilson and Emma Thompson together and you'll give anything a go, even if it's terrible. Luckily for us, Down Cemetery Road is far from terrible. The British series, which has episodes dropping weekly, introduces us to Oxfordshire-based classic art restorer Sarah (Wilson) who becomes obsessed with finding a child injured in a house explosion neighbouring her property. Her fixation starts innocently enough, as she is simply trying to pass along a handmade 'get well soon' card to the kid from one of the other children in the neighbourhood. But she's stopped at the hospital and asked to leave. Then she finds press coverage of the explosion has edited the child out of the narrative. Her final straw is when police say information on the injured girl has been flagged and cannot be shared. So she hires a private investigator to look into the perplexing situation, driven by a need to know what's going on. That puts her on contact with Thompson's no-nonsense Zoe. She's capable, witty and not one for keeping with tradition. And as with any Thompson character, you can't help but like her immediately. The series is from the creator of the celebrated Slow Horses , and looks set to be an engaging, enjoyable mystery with a good deal of humour and quirks to complement the intrigue and darkness. ALSO STREAMING Connie Nielsen and Sean Bean in Robin Hood. Picture by Stan The famed archer of Nottingham is back for another iteration with Stan's new modernised retelling of Robin Hood . The period series stars Sean Bean and Connie Nielsen. There's plenty of new content on Netflix, with Colin Farrell poker drama Ballad of a Small Player; Aussie Superwog spin-off series Son of a Donkey ; the return of fantasy series The Witcher , now with Aussie Liam Hemsworth taking over the Geralt role from Henry Cavill; and Aileen: Queen of the Serial Killers , a documentary film about Aileen Wuornos, who was portrayed by Charlize Theron in the Oscar-winning film Monster . Over on Paramount+ Tracy Morgan leads new sitcom Crutch , a spin-off from The Neighbourhood . And on Prime Video you'll find Hedda , writer-director Nia DaCosta's new take on the classic Henrik Ibsen play Hedda Gabler, with Tessa Thompson in the lead. While the believability of just about everything in this show is thin at best, it does make for fun and engaging drama, especially when paired with the incredibly liberal use of slow-motion cinematography and off-kilter camera angles. This season also continues Lydia's struggle to be taken seriously by her and James' insufferably villainous father, as well as her little bun in the oven situation. But like any high school romance show, Maxton Hall lives and dies by its leads' chemistry, and Herbig-Matten and Hardung have it through the roof. Existing fans will love this season as much as the first, and won't be able to wait for season three. Ruth Wilson and Emma Thompson in Down Cemetery Road. Picture by AppleTV+ DOWN CEMETERY ROAD AppleTV+ Pair Ruth Wilson and Emma Thompson together and you'll give anything a go, even if it's terrible. Luckily for us, Down Cemetery Road is far from terrible. The British series, which has episodes dropping weekly, introduces us to Oxfordshire-based classic art restorer Sarah (Wilson) who becomes obsessed with finding a child injured in a house explosion neighbouring her property. Her fixation starts innocently enough, as she is simply trying to pass along a handmade 'get well soon' card to the kid from one of the other children in the neighbourhood. But she's stopped at the hospital and asked to leave. Then she finds press coverage of the explosion has edited the child out of the narrative. Her final straw is when police say information on the injured girl has been flagged and cannot be shared. So she hires a private investigator to look into the perplexing situation, driven by a need to know what's going on. That puts her on contact with Thompson's no-nonsense Zoe. She's capable, witty and not one for keeping with tradition. And as with any Thompson character, you can't help but like her immediately. The series is from the creator of the celebrated Slow Horses , and looks set to be an engaging, enjoyable mystery with a good deal of humour and quirks to complement the intrigue and darkness. ALSO STREAMING Connie Nielsen and Sean Bean in Robin Hood. Picture by Stan The famed archer of Nottingham is back for another iteration with Stan's new modernised retelling of Robin Hood . The period series stars Sean Bean and Connie Nielsen. There's plenty of new content on Netflix, with Colin Farrell poker drama Ballad of a Small Player; Aussie Superwog spin-off series Son of a Donkey ; the return of fantasy series The Witcher , now with Aussie Liam Hemsworth taking over the Geralt role from Henry Cavill; and Aileen: Queen of the Serial Killers , a documentary film about Aileen Wuornos, who was portrayed by Charlize Theron in the Oscar-winning film Monster . Over on Paramount+ Tracy Morgan leads new sitcom Crutch , a spin-off from The Neighbourhood . And on Prime Video you'll find Hedda , writer-director Nia DaCosta's new take on the classic Henrik Ibsen play Hedda Gabler, with Tessa Thompson in the lead. Henson To Star In Motivational New Netflix Drama ‘Tis So Sweet’ The Oscar-nominated actress teams up with Tyler Perry and DeVon Franklin for a moving true story about faith, healing, and second chances. Taraji P. Henson By Okla Jones · Updated October 30, 2025 Getting your Trinity Audio player ready… Taraji P. Henson is stepping into one of her most heartfelt roles yet. The Academy Award–nominated actress will lead ’Tis So Sweet , an upcoming Netflix drama inspired by the true story of Lenore Lindsey, a Chicago bakery owner whose life changes after an extraordinary discovery forces her to confront the past and rediscover her faith, healing, and purpose. Set against the rich backdrop of the city’s South Side, this project promises to blend soulful storytelling with the emotional depth that has made Henson a staple in Black culture, and the film industry overall. of her generation. Tis So Sweet will be directed by Tasha Smith, adapted from a screenplay by Randy Brown ( Miracles From Heaven ). The film also stars recording artist, actor, and ESSENCE cover star Joey Bada$$, expanding the story’s emotional range with a multigenerational ensemble cast. Behind the scenes, DeVon Franklin and Tyler Perry will produce, with Tony Strickland and Angi Bones serving as executive producers for Tyler Perry Studios, alongside Bart Lipton. Tyler Perry, Photo by Prince Williams/ DeVon Franklin Courtesy of Netflix The film marks the second release from Tyler Perry and DeVon Franklin’s ongoing partnership with Netflix to create uplifting, faith-based stories for global audiences. Their first collaboration, Ruth & Boaz , reimagined a biblical tale in a modern Southern setting and quickly became a breakout hit, debuting at No. 2 on Netflix’s Global Top 10 Movies List. Production is expected to begin later this year, with Netflix set to release the film in 2026. TOPICS: Joey Bada$$ Netflix Taraji P. Henson Tyler Perry

Henson To lead Peacock TV Show Based on 50 Cent Novel November 3, 2025 By Anubhav Chaudhry Peacock has reportedly added a new drama series led by Taraji P. Henson to its upcoming slate. The project is based on a recent novel by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and marks a collaboration between their production banners. Early details suggest it will blend crime, power, and moral conflict in a high-stakes story. Taraji P. Henson cast in Peacock’s TV show adaptation of 50 Cent novel Taraji P. Henson will star in and executive-produce Peacock’s television adaptation of The Accomplice, a crime novel by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and Aaron Philip Clark. The project, produced by Universal Content Productions, is currently in development with Jackson’s G-Unit Films and Television and Henson’s TPH Entertainment attached. No writer has been announced for the series (via Variety ). According to the official logline, Henson will play Nia Adams, a fearless Texas Ranger chasing master thief Desmond Bell. His latest heist targets one of America’s wealthiest families. As Adams closes in, she uncovers a web of corruption that forces her to choose between revealing the truth and protecting the system she swore to uphold. Jackson released the novel in 2024, and the show marks Henson’s second collaboration with Peacock after Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist. Both Henson and Jackson serve as non-writing executive producers on the series. Jackson’s upcoming projects include Fightland for Starz, the home of his Power franchise. The universe spans multiple spin-offs, including Power Book II: Ghost, Power Book III: Raising Kanan, and Power Book IV: Force. He is also developing Hip Hop Cop for Hulu and a Netflix docuseries about Sean “Diddy” Combs. Henson, known for her roles in Empire and Hidden Figures, recently signed a first-look deal with Fox Entertainment Studios to develop scripted and unscripted projects. She also holds a two-picture film deal with Netflix (via Deadline ). Her recent credits include The Color Purple and Think Like a Man Too. She has earned multiple Emmy nominations and an Academy Award nomination for The Curious Case of Benjamin Button. The Accomplice continues Peacock’s expansion into original, character-driven drama series. Henson & More Join Cast October 30, 2025 By Carly Levy Tyler Perry struck a Netflix deal with producer DeVon Franklin to bring faith-based movies to the streaming service. So far, their first movie together was Ruth & Boaz , which followed a hip-hop artist looking to start over in rural Tennessee. But their collaboration is far from over with Perry and Franklin’s next faith-based movie starring Taraji P. Henson and more. DeVon Franklin and Tyler Perry truly make a great team for constantly incorporating faith into their films. Franklin produces faith-based movies like Miracles From Heaven, Heaven Is For Real, and Breakthrough, all about the power of belief when it seems like all hope is lost. Tyler Perry has also never shied away from his inclusion of faith, even in his most hilarious works. His first movie, Diary of a Mad Black Woman, had a powerful message about the strength of forgiveness. There was also I Can Do Bad All By Myself, which taught the importance of helping others. As their first collaboration, Ruth & Boaz, debuted at #2 on the Global Top 10 Movies List (English), these two producers bring to Netflix stories of faith and compassion. What is Tyler Perry’s new movie about? According to Deadline , Tyler Perry and DeVon Franklin are co-producing ‘Tis So Sweet, the true story of Lenore Lindsey. Directed by Tasha Smith , a Chicago bakery owner makes a miraculous discovery that helps her take back lost time, heal old wounds, and find unexpected purpose. Taraji P. Henson, who’s starred in four of Perry’s movies, will lead again for the upcoming Netflix movie. She also plans to star alongside her frequent director in Why Did I Get Married Again?, a Netflix sequel to 2007’s Why Did I Get Married? Rapper/actor Jo-Vaughn Virginie Scott (a.k.a. Joey Bada$$) is also cast, who appeared in shows like Mr. Robot, Grown-ish, and Power Book III: Raising Kanan. Check in for more casting and release date news for ‘Tis So Sweet, set to be available on Netflix. Carly Levy Carly Levy is movie news writer born and raised in South Florida. As a hardcore cinephile, her Mount Rushmore of film directors includes Wes Anderson, John Carney, James Cameron, and Robert Wise. She has a knack for analyzing every movie she sees and isn't afraid to voice her thoughts on it. DeVon Franklin Joey Basa$$ Movie News Netflix Taraji P. Henson and co-hosted with her long time best friend Tracie Jade Jenkins, who is the Executive Director of Henson’s Boris Lawrence Henson Foundation . In the new original series, Golden Globe Award-Winning Actress Taraji P. Henson and Tracie Jade Jenkins will shine a spotlight on the challenging mental health issues facing us today – particularly of those in the Black community. Through personal interviews with both celebrities, experts and everyday people, the series will show how to provide support, bring awareness and help eliminate the stigmas of mental health issues. Each episode will focus on a different mental health topic with multiple content drops per week. Henson founded The Boris Lawrence Foundation in 2018, a nonprofit organization led by Tracie Jade Jenkins. Oscars Grammys Golden Globes Box Office Digital Magazines Gold Derby Q&A Craig Brewer celebrates 20 years of ‘Hustle & Flow,’ the Oscar-winning ‘miracle’ nobody wanted to make Two decades after his breakout hit, the director looks back on the film that changed his life, launched Terrence Howard and Taraji P. Henson, and made Three 6 Mafia Oscar winners. By Denton Davidson Plus icon Denton Davidson More stories by Denton ‘A Useful Ghost’: How a haunted vacuum cleaner became Thailand’s funniest (and most moving) awards contender 0 Comments Read more ‘The Voice of Hind Rajab’ drops trailer: Everything to know about Tunisia’s Gaza-set Oscar contender 0 Comments Read more Park Chan-wook on past Oscar snubs — and why ‘No Other Choice’ could be his golden invitation 0 Comments Read more November 10, 2025 8:00 am Taraji P. Henson, Paula Jai Parker, Terrence Howard, and Taryn Manning in Hustle & Flow Paramount/Courtesy Everett Collection Share Share on Facebook Post google Google Preferred Pin it Show more sharing options Share to Flipboard Post to Tumblr Submit to Reddit Share on LinkedIn Share on WhatsApp Email Print This Page 0 When Craig Brewer thinks back on Hustle & Flow, one word still comes to mind: miracle. “I’ve been thinking about what a miracle the movie is — that no one wanted to make it,” Brewer tells Gold Derby. “Rest his soul, John Singleton putting his house up for collateral, financing the movie for $2 million, and us just being out here in the Memphis heat making this movie with these newish actors — Terrence Howard , Taraji P. Henson , this new rapper on the scene, Ludacris . And somehow it all came together.” A movie no one wanted to make When Hustle & Flow premiered at the 2005 Sundance Film Festival, it was the definition of an underdog story — a gritty, Memphis-made drama about a small-time hustler who dreams of becoming a rapper. Brewer remembers constant rejection before Singleton, a two-time Oscar nominee for Boyz n the Hood , decided to back the film himself. Related Stories Matt and Ross Duffer tease Max’s fate in ‘Stranger Things 5’: ‘It’ll surprise people how she comes into the show’ GG Hawkins on her ‘crazy leap’: How she made the unconventional ‘I Really Love My Husband’ on a micro-budget “There was a lot of resistance to Hustle & Flow ,” Brewer recalls. “People were saying, ‘Should we care about a pimp rapping?’ But John believed in it. He knew about Three 6 Mafia , he knew what Southern rap was doing. He just got it.” Director Craig Brewer, producers Stephanie Allain, and John Singleton on set Paramount/courtesy Everett Collection That faith changed everything. The film went on to sell to Paramount in a $9 million distribution deal, earn two Oscar nominations, and deliver one of the most unforgettable Academy Award moments of the 2000s — when Three 6 Mafia won Best Original Song for “It’s Hard Out Here for a Pimp.” “Those guys didn’t have a touch of cynicism in them,” he says of rap group. “They stormed the stage in their street clothes, platinum grills shining, and just screamed with joy. Nobody was ready for that — but it was infectious.” After the ceremony, Brewer found himself at an after-party only Hollywood could produce. “I got invited to Prince ’s house,” he laughs. “There was a river of chocolate you could dip fruit into, Sheila E. was performing — it was absolutely wild. Ludacris grabbed me and said, ‘Do you know what this means for us? Three 6 Mafia just won an Academy Award.’ He was right. It was a big deal for the Southern rap scene.” Two stars are born For Brewer, one of the joys of revisiting Hustle & Flow two decades later is seeing how far his cast has come. The film marked a major turning point for both Terrence Howard and Taraji P. Henson, whose chemistry as DJay and Shug helped make the film a phenomenon. 'Hustle & Flow': Terrence Howard, Taraji P. Henson Paramount/courtesy Everett Collection Both actors went on to become fixtures in Hollywood: Howard earned an Oscar nomination for Hustle & Flow and later starred in Empire, reuniting with Henson, who became one of television’s most commanding presences and earned her own Oscar nod for The Curious Case of Benjamin Button in 2009. Brewer even reconnected with them on last year's Peacock limited series Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist. “When Taraji got involved, I was so excited,” Brewer says. “But then Will Packer gave me a call and he’s like, ‘I don’t think we’re done. I think we need to go get your boy.’ I was like, ‘Are you really serious? You want me to go get Terrence?’ I remember calling up Terrence and saying, ‘All right, you know I love you. You know that I’m going to get out of your way and I’m going to give you everything that you want. I just want you to show up and give me everything you got.’” He laughs, recalling Howard’s unique on-set energy. “I’ll never forget him saying, ‘Well, I’ll tell you what I see. I see the Bee Gees. I want a Bee Gee wig.’ He had this long chestnut wavy wig that he just never wanted to take off. He wore it to the premiere.” Terrence Howard as Cadillac Richie in 'Fight Night: The Million Dollar Heist' Eli Joshua Adé/Peacock Still echoing through Memphis Two decades later, Hustle & Flow continues to reverberate across Brewer’s hometown. “You can’t go to a Memphis Grizzlies game without hearing 20,000 people chant ‘Whoop That Trick,’” he says proudly. “I’m talking old blue-haired ladies shouting it — and meaning it. It’s scary to the opposing team.” The chant, based on the film’s breakout anthem, has become a cultural calling card for Memphis — a symbol of pride, persistence, and scrappy energy. A family that never broke up The Hustle & Flow family, Brewer says, never really disbanded. “We’re all still very close,” he says. “ Al Kapone , who wrote ‘Whoop That Trick’ — everybody in Three 6 — we still all connect regularly. Elise Neal , who is in the movie, is a Memphis resident now. We hang out. Not only that, but there were strippers that were in our movie from 2005 that I had made my first movie with in 1999 ( The Poor & Hungry ). We go to kid birthdays and barbecues, and that’s just the way we do things here in Memphis. So, it’s a family that’s still together, I’m happy to say.” Singleton passed away in 2019, but Brewer still feels his presence. “I miss him a lot,” he says. “I wish he could have seen my next movie. I was really fortunate that he got to see an early cut of Dolemite Is My Name before he passed away. But Hustle & Flow is a special movie that has remained for a long time in people’s minds and the culture." How it connects to ‘Song Sung Blue’ Twenty years after Hustle & Flow, Brewer is once again returning to the world of dreamers and music with Song Sung Blue , his upcoming film starring Hugh Jackman and Kate Hudson , opening Christmas Day. The film follows a working-class Milwaukee couple who perform in a Neil Diamond tribute band — and Brewer sees more than a few echoes between the two stories. “I hope everybody sees Song Sung Blue because it’s a little bit of a brother to Hustle & Flow, I feel,” he says. Kate Hudson and Hugh Jackman in Song Sung Blue Focus Features Both films, he explains, are about ordinary people trying to channel pain and hope into art. Where DJay built beats in a sweltering Memphis basement, Mike and Claire sing their hearts out under cheap stage lights — chasing something bigger than fame. “I love movies about people who are trying to start over,” Brewer says. “They not only want to do something different in their career and make this tribute band, but they also want to get married. They also want to see if they can start a family again after failure in that realm before.” The legacy For Brewer, Hustle & Flow remains a turning point that shaped both his life and career. The relationships forged on that set — from Singleton to the cast and crew he still calls family — continue to anchor his work two decades later. “It was a miracle the movie got made — and somehow, it all came together,” Brewer says . The film helped define his path as a filmmaker and strengthened his bond with the city that first believed in him. Memphis still chants the film’s anthem at basketball games, and Brewer still calls its people his creative home. Read More: Craig Brewer FYC Hustle & Flow Paramount Song Sung Blue Taraji P. Having written over 300 articles in just over a year, Billy regularly covers the biggest TV shows and films releasing while also analysing some of the most underrated properties that may slip your attention. Having studied for an MA in Screenwriting at UAL in 2023, Billy honed his writing skills and also developed his ability to critique the work of other creative minds. Before that, Billy studied politics at the University of Nottingham, which helped him to bring nuanced and scholarly analysis to the frameworks within which filmmakers and writers have framed their thematic messages. Obviously, not in real life. That's how birthdays, Christmases, and Thanksgivings end with a cake or turkey on the floor. However, in TV and film, those close interpersonal conflicts can breed some of the most dramatic and thrilling confrontations that have audiences begging for more. Just think about how Game of Thrones , Succession , and even Keeping Up With the Kardashians thrive off the battles, fictional or non-fictional, between those related by blood and outsiders who ruin that family dynamic. Well, if you are looking for a show that is every bit as wild and bingeable as those, look no further than Empire . This 5-season drama has almost everything a binge-watcher could ask for. Almost unbelievable plots, politicking, violence, sex, comedy, fantastic performances, and influential soundtracks. Not only did it help resurrect careers, but it showcased how the TV and music industries could interlink in real life, blurring two different kinds of artistry. With over 100 episodes to get through, Empire is a show that not only deserves your attention but will command it for weeks on end. 'Empire' Follows the Lyon Family Hip-Hop Dynasty If someone were to ask how to describe Empire , the most succinct way possible would be that it was Succession before Succession . Perhaps not in terms of critical success, but certainly in terms of its premise. Empire follows the Lyon family as its patriarch, Lucious ( Terrence Howard ), decides who will take over the family business , the Empire music label that he built. Though, like Logan Roy ( Brian Cox ), he sees his options as limited. There is Andre ( Trai Byers ), who isn't musically talented like the other Lyons but acts as the consigliere of the family with his legal and business acumen; Jamal ( Jussie Smollett ), who feels like he was inspired by Pharrell Williams , though is looked down upon for his homosexuality by his father; and Hakeem ( Bryshere Y. Gray ), who is more interested in emulating his father's gangster background than acting like an adult. Among all of this is Cookie ( Taraji P. Henson ), Lucious' ex-wife, who loves her children but also seeks to place herself as the one pulling the strings behind the scenes. With this, the stakes go beyond just business and familial relationships to attempted murder. Lines are crossed with complicated relationships that cross boundaries, as Lucious struggles to let go of his power and seeks to prove he is still the dominant force, even if he is not the one directly in control. Yet, under all the scheming and betrayals, there is still the heartache of each character loving their family and feeling they are forced to play this brutal game , with all the children really just wanting their father's approval. 'Empire' Features Fantastic Performances and Revived Terrence Howard's Career Taraji P. Henson as Cookie Lyon in 'Empire' Image via Fox With the almost over-the-top arcs these characters embark on, such as Hakeem stealing his own father's fiancée, Anika ( Grace Byers ), at one point, it would be easy for their performances to feel lacking in weight. However, this could not be further from the case. Despite the pair of them being mired in controversy and rightly condemned for some of their actions and words in recent years, it is impossible not to acknowledge how Smollett and Howard bring a necessary gravitas to their roles, especially with the complexity of their relationship as a gay son and a homophobic father . Empire was even credited with helping to revive Howard's career as a leading man following his departure from Marvel after Iron Man , even if the actor would go on to ruin his image again with further assault allegations and bogus pseudo-science claims. Related The 83 Best TV Shows to Binge Watch Right Now From 'Succession' and 'Barry' to 'Stranger Things' and 'Breaking Bad,' here are the best shows to binge — and where to watch them. Posts 3 By Matt Goldberg Apr 29, 2010 However, the true star of Empire is undoubtedly Henson as Cookie, which won Henson a Golden Globe for "Best Performance by an Actress In A Television Series." Henson plays the character as witty yet also intensely petty and sometimes cruel, with one-liners such as summing up Hakeem's entire character with "You need to stop rappin' like you from the streets, 'cause you not about that life!" or shutting down Lucious' advances on her by saying "Get rid of fake-ass Halle Berry. As long as she's around, I'm closed for business." With these lines, Henson doesn't just make the audience laugh with her sassy and snappy delivery, but plays a similar role to Cersei ( Lena Headey ) in later seasons of Game of Thrones , where there is something delightful about watching a woman outdo the men around her in a male-dominated world. She can even be unnecessarily blunt, telling Jamal that, "For a queen, you sure do keep a messy place. What you need is a good maid up in here." While a borderline homophobic thing to say, the context of Cookie's persona and love for her children keeps her sympathetic rather than making us hate her. 'Empire' Changed How Music Was Viewed in TV Hakeem, Jamal, Cookie, and Lucious singing in the studio in Empire Image via FOX Being a show about musicians trying to take over a record label, Empire comes with some absolute bangers that are original songs from the actors that went far beyond the show's fanbase. In 2015, the Season 1 soundtrack hit #1 on the Billboard charts , the first to do so since Glee , which featured cover music . Incorporating this into the show, from boardrooms to recording booths, meant there was a versatility to Empire’s success and tone not often seen on today’s television. Some shows do attempt to replicate it, such as how The Witcher saw success with Joey Batey 's recordings of songs like "Toss a Coin to Your Witcher," and "Burn Butcher Burn," which have over 100 million and 46 million streams on Spotify, respectively. But Empire paved the way for this kind of creative experimentation. While some may consider Empire to be a guilty pleasure, considering the dramatized nature of the characters and world they exist within, which sets it apart from the more grounded and nuanced world of Succession , there is no reason why you shouldn't embrace said pleasure. Cookie certainly wouldn't blame you. With some standout performances and trailblazing history, Empire isn't like many 5-season shows you'll watch, and that makes it all the juicier for your binge satisfaction.
