The University of Cumbria has played a pivotal role in shaping a landmark set of international guidelines for rewilding that have been launched at the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) World Conservation Congress 2025 in Abu Dhabi. It is an event that takes place every four years and brings together thousands of organisations, scientists, policy experts, business leaders and professionals from around the globe to help set the agenda for future nature conservation. Developed by the Rewilding Thematic Group of the IUCN Commission on Ecosystem Management (CEM), the new guidelines offer an evidence-informed framework for restoring ecosystems worldwide. Logos for IUCN CEM Thematic Group (Image: University of Cumbria) Professor Ian Convery, co-chair of the IUCN CEM Rewilding Thematic Group and Professor of Environment & Society at the University of Cumbria, co-authored the guidelines alongside a global team of experts. The team also included Sally Hawkins who is a former University of Cumbria postgraduate researcher now working in Australia. The guidelines reflect contributions from over 60 organisations and hundreds of practitioners, policymakers, scientists, and community representatives. “It’s been a privilege to help shape global rewilding policy through the IUCN,” said Professor Convery, who describes rewilding as a ‘bold yet pragmatic approach to ecological restoration’. “The University of Cumbria’s work, from the Back On Our Map (BOOM) project’s species restoration to our pine marten reintroduction in South Cumbria, shows how research, policy and place-based action can work hand in hand. These new IUCN guidelines capture that same ethos, combining science, inclusivity and optimism to restore thriving landscapes for people and nature.” The University of Cumbria’s Institute of Science and Environment (IoSE) research and applied projects have helped inform the development of rewilding practice. They include the BOOM project, which ran until 2024 and successfully restored locally extinct species across South Cumbria. It has reconnected fragmented habitats and engaging communities in nature recovery. Building on that legacy, the South Cumbria Pine Marten Recovery Project is now re-establishing a self-sustaining pine marten population, strengthening ecosystem function and deepening local involvement. Pine martens were eleased into Grizedale Forest and Rusland Valley to aid conservation (Image: Supplied) A Professor of Conservation Science, Professor Robert (Bob) Montgomery is Director of the Centre for National Parks and Protected Areas and also Director of Research and Knowledge Exchange in the Institute of Science and Environment at the University of Cumbria. Professor Montgomery said: “This collaboration provides yet another example of the stalwart ways in which the University of Cumbria is developing and driving partnerships globally to protect the integrity of coupled human and natural systems.” The IUCN CEM guidelines on rewilding recognise the diversity of rewilding approaches worldwide, while articulating a shared vision for rewilding. Grounded in ecological science and informed by social science insights, they provide a flexible framework that can be adapted to various environmental, cultural and governance contexts. The IUCN CEM rewilding guidelines can be found at https://portals.iucn.org/library/node/52582 The IUCN 2025 World Conservation Congress ran until 15 October, 2025 Nature Share 0 Comments Get involved with the news Send your news & photos Loading... text: Blue Jasmine | The Arts Desk Skip to main content thu 27/11/2025 Sections Search today new music opera film classical theatre comedy dance visual arts tv gaming CD/DVDs Books Search form Search Main navigation today new music opera film classical theatre comedy dance visual arts tv gaming cd/dvds books Search Secondary menu reviews features gallery q & a proms first person we recommend Breadcrumb Home Film Blue Jasmine reviews, news & interviews Blue Jasmine Not like Woody Allen's early funny ones, but one of his later best by Karen Krizanovich Monday, September 23, 2013 share this article Share An update on Tennessee Williams’ A Streetcare Named Desire , it isn’t essential to have seen that work on stage to enjoy this pithy homage from Woody Allen. However, revisiting the iconic 1951 film version starring Marlon Brando, Vivien Leigh and Kim Hunter could very well make Blue Jasmine even funnier. This is because Allen treats the audience as equals to the tragic in-joke of familial impact and the damage left in its wake. The pivot is a beautiful woman’s perpetually occurring emotional meltdown. Former wealthy Manhattan socialite Jasmine (Cate Blanchett) is the Blanche character, a tall, blonde, Hermès bag-carrying emotional steamroller who flattens everything of which she doesn’t approve and who only submits to lower the eschelon when must needs. Showing up at her estranged adopted sister Ginger’s cramped San Francisco apartment, Jasmine criticises everything she sees – from her sister’s fat children, to her loud boyfriend. Ginger (Sally Hawkins, with a respectable American accent) may be impressionable but she’s no pushover. Having had Jasmine ruin her previous marriage by bankrupting her and her then-husband Augie (Andrew Dice Clay, pictured below with Hawkins) with a bad property deal, Ginger is ready to forgive if not forget. Her current beau Chili (Bobby Cannavale) is the working-class Cassandra, warning Ginger of the damaging ideas of her sister. In typical Allen style, Woody keeps the story tight and the pace brisk. Questionable decisions are made and we grit our teeth for both Jasmine and Ginger. While we’re not surprised at the fallout, we are surprised at the final result: Allen may have pitched this tale with a predictable arc but he uses both the narrative and the actors like surgical tools to show us something familiar and tragically funny. Cate Blanchett has never been sharper, both as a solo performer and in ensemble. Her skill at being awkward, crazy and credible allows her to reveal Jasmine’s painful past with surgical precision. This is a film that doesn’t mince words or waste time, much as Jasmine relies on the kindness of men with money. Although Blanchett steals the show, supporting performances are equally indelible – and it must be said this is one of Woody’s best-cast works of his entire filmography. Peter Sarsgaard fills the shoes of the too perfect East Coast diplomat and political aspirant. Hal, Jasmine’s wealthy ex-husband, gives Alec Baldwin a character he can fully inhabit, while comedians Dice Clay and Louis C.K. get to show their incredible skill with drama – after all, comedy is harder. A story of the 1 percent vs the 99 percent in the same family, even if sans DNA (both sisters were adopted), Blue Jasmine is a heartbreakingly funny take on aspirations gone wrong at a level where it shouldn’t happen but does. It also illustrates the moral of following your own advice – and in that way, leaves us leaving the cinema with a good taste in our mouths if a fissure in our hearts. Ultimately, Blue Jasmine is not Woody Allen at his early funniest, but it is Woody Allen at his later best. Discuss Now St. Denis Medical Season 2 on NBC (Image via YouTube/NBC) St. Denis Medical Season 2 is here, and the cast is bringing on the heart and humor! The mockumentary style hospital comedy series revolves around the lives of doctors and nurses in an unfunded hospital in Oregon. St. Denis Medical Season 2 cast includes Wendi McLendon-Covey, Mekki Leeper, Allison Tolman, Kaliko Kauahi, Josh Lawson, David Alan Grier, Kahyun Kim, Kristen Schaal, Lauren Weedman, and Frankie Quiñones among others. The season premiered with two episodes on NBC on November 3, 2025. The episodes can be streamed on Peacock as well. In the first season, which premiered in 2024, the audience is introduced to the colorful characters at the St. Denis Medical . Executive director Joyce is desperately trying to keep the hospital afloat. Things take a turn when she gets an exorbitant amount as funds. She finds herself caught in a chaotic mess as she tries to figure out how to use the money wisely. At the end of the season, she decides to build a birthing center. Meanwhile, the other characters find themselves juggling between their work and personal life challenges. St. Denis Medical Season 2 will take the story forward, bringing forth the daily struggles of an understaffed medical team as they try to do their best in the circumstances. The series is co-created by Eric Ledgin and Justin Spitzer. St. Denis Medical Season 2 Cast Wendi McLendon-Covey as Joyce – Joyce is the executive director at the hospital, who is often seen struggling to handle crisis at the workplace. Wendi McLendon-Covey is also known for her roles in The Goldbergs , Reno 911! And Bridesmaids . David Alan Grier as Ron – A seasoned medical professional, Ron seems up have a lot up his sleeves at work and in his personal life. David Alan Grier has also appeared in The Color Purple and Candy Cane Lane. Allison Tolman as Alex – In St. Denis Medical Season 2, Allison Tolman plays the role of Alex, the supervising nurse, who is central to the hospital’s ecosystem. Allison Tolman has been part of other projects such as Brooklyn Nine-Nine, Fargo and Good Girls. Josh Lawson as Bruce – Dr. Bruce plays the role of the arrogant surgeon at the hospital. Josh Lawson has also appeared in Superstore . Kahyun Kim as Serena – In St. Denis Medical Season 2, Kahyun Kim plays the role of nurse Serena. Kim has also appeared in Cocaine Bear . Mekki Leeper as Matt – Matt is a new nurse on the block, whose upbringing makes him difficult to fit in. Mekki Leeper has also appeared in The S*x Live of College Girls and Jury Duty . Kaliko Kauahi as Val – A nurse administrator, Val is the one who helps keep the chaos at bay in the hospital. Kaliko Kauahi has also appeared in Superstore and Parks and Recreation . Guest stars on St. Denis Medical Season 2 Ariana Madix as Dr. Emerson – Ariana will play the guest role of Dr. Emerson. Madix is known for hosting Love Island USA and has appeared on Vanderpump Rules . Adam Rippon in unknown character – Adam will play the role of a patient, getting treated by Dr. Bruce. Adam Rippon is an Olympic figure skater. Paul Scheer as Ruben – In St. Denis Medical Season 2, Ruben’s brother needs a transplant. He will be part of a heartfelt narrative to do with family and heath support. Paul Scheer is also known for The League and Black Monday. Jessica Lowe as Violet – Violet comes to hospital looking for her ex-husband. Jessica Lowe has also been in The Righteous Gemstones . Wayne Knight as Dr. Axler – Dr. Axler is a cardiologist, who finds in nemesis at the hospital. Wayne Knight is known for his roles in Seinfeld and Jurassic Park . Jeremiah Brown as Jeff – Jeff will play the role of an athlete who is at the hospital awaiting his friend to be discharged. Jeremiah Brown has appeared on Love Island USA . Kristen Schaal as Ashley – In St. Denis Medical Season 2, Ashley, a sci-fi fan, is expected to bring some fun energy to the screen as she will have a surprising encounter with someone at the hospital. Kristen Schaal has also been part of What We Do in the Shadows and Bob’s Burgers . Lauren Weedman as Pam – Pam is a retired nurse who is called back to Dr. Denis Medical because of the hospital being short-staffed. Lauren Weedman is also known for her roles in Hacks and Sirens. Frankie Quiñones as Leslie – Leslie is a security guard, who seems to know a lot about the happenings at the hospital. Frankie Quiñones has appeared in What We Do in the Shadows and This Fool. Lauren Lapkus in unknown character – In St. Denis Medical Season 2, Lauren is expected to play the role of a pregnant woman, who arrives at the hospital with her husband played by Tim Baltz. Lauren Lapkus has been part of other successful shows such as The Wrong Missy and The Big Bang Theory . Tim Baltz in unknown character – Tim will portray the role of Lauren’s husband. They turn up at the hospital after something goes wrong with their gender reveal party. Tim Baltz is also known for his roles in The Righteous Gemstones and Driver’s Ed Jonah Beckett as Kyle – In St. Denis Medical Season 2, Kyle turns up at the hospital with a strange illness. Jonah Beckett was last seen in HBO Max series The S*x Live of College Girls . Watch St. Denis Medical Season 2 on NBC. The episodes will be available to stream on Peacock the next day. Disney+ released the new trailer for the upcoming season of the series based on Rick Riordan ‘s beloved bestselling books on Thursday. This season follows the events of the series’ second book in the Percy Jackson series, The Sea of Monsters . It promises to have higher stakes, even more action and thrilling new monsters. “After Camp Half-Blood’s protective border is breached, Percy Jackson embarks on an epic odyssey into the Sea of Monsters in search of his best friend Grover and the one thing that may save the camp — the legendary Golden Fleece,” according to its official synopsis. “With help from Annabeth, Clarisse and his newfound cyclops half-brother Tyson, Percy’s survival becomes essential to stopping Luke, the Titan Kronos, and their impending plan to bring down Camp Half-Blood — and ultimately, Olympus.” Walker Scobell once again stars as the titular son of Poseidon. Leah Sava Jeffries and Aryan Simhadri also star as Annabeth Chase and Grover. Charlie Bushnell , Dior Goodjohn and Daniel Diemer make up the rest of the main cast, while a star-studded cast of recurring and guest stars includes Lin-Manuel Miranda , Jason Mantzoukas , Timothy Simons , Courtney B. Vance , Andra Day , Margaret Cho and Kristen Schaal . “You guys get nightmares, right?” Scobell’s Percy asks in the trailer. “I usually get ones that tell me the future. Or, try to kill me.” Percy Jackson and the Olympians season 2 premieres with two episodes on Dec. 10. New episodes will debut every Wednesday. Disney is the parent company of ABC News. Sign in to your ScreenRant account Summary Generate a summary of this story follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap As the premiere date draws closer, fans now have a clearer look at the second season of Percy Jackson and the Olympians from Disney+, with a new trailer just released. Adapting the plot of Rick Riordan's second Percy Jackson book, The Sea of Monsters , season 2 will see Percy (Walker Scobell) and Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries) going on a rogue quest to save Camp Half-Blood. They are joined by Percy's recently-discovered half-brother Tyson (new cast member Daniel Diemer), and fellow demigod/frenemy Clarisse (Dior Goodjohn). Charlie Bushnell will also reprise his role as Luke, while other actors joining the cast include Courtney B. Vance, Sandra Bernhard, Kristen Schaal, Margaret Cho, Rosemarie DeWitt, Kevin Chacon, Beatrice Kitsos, and Tamara Smart. Check out the new trailer for Percy Jackson and the Olympians season 2, which premieres on Disney+ on December 10: As teased by the new trailer, Percy's new quest will intersect with having to rescue Grover (Aryan Simhadri), while further clashing with Luke, who is leading a rebellion of demigods against the Olympians. Lin-Manuel Miranda also reappears as Luke's father Hermes, as well as Toby Stephens as Percy's father Poseidon, and Virginia Kull as his mother Sally. But Disney only reveals glimpses of some of the most intriguing new characters, such as C.C. (DeWitt), a mysterious figure who runs a spa in the middle of the Sea of Monsters. More of the biggest action set pieces of the second installment are also unveiled, such as the dangerous chariot race at Camp Half-Blood allowed under cruel interim activities director Tantalus ( Veep 's Timothy Simmons). Percy Jackson season 2 will also set up the next installment, as characters from the third book, The Titan's Curse , have already been cast. Jon Benjamin Jokes That ‘Bob’s Burgers’ Is Still Popular Because It Helps Put People To Sleep Is 'Bob's Burgers' just animated Ambien? November 06, 2025 Add Cracked to Google Keegan Kelly Of all the qualities that audiences have long ascribed to H. Jon Benjamin’s glorious voice, he might be the first person to ever call it “soporific.” There have never been more tools available to the poor sleepers of the world that don’t require them to put away their phones than there are right now. ASMR videos, white noise apps, 14-hour YouTube meditation playlists, the list goes on and on – hell, there’s even a dedicated community of Frasier fans debating which stretch of episodes has the most soothing high-brow antics for a sophisticated insomniac. Then, there’s Bob’s Burgers . In a recent cast and crew panel at New York Comic Con, an interviewer from Buzzfeed asked the talent behind the sixteen-seasons-and-counting animated sitcom to opine on why they think Bob’s Burgers continues to be so popular so far into its run, and the series star suggested that the show's ability to lunch-lull its viewers to sleep could be behind their massive success. Don't Miss 6 Insanely Tone-Deaf Ways The WWE Addressed Serious Issues Authors Steve Hanley Published 05/09/2015 6 Movies You Won't Believe Are Based on Insane True Stories Authors Robin Warder Published 09/24/2013 22 of the Best Bad Movies Authors Amanda Mannen Published 11/26/2025 And here Hulu thought that Bob's Burgers fans just loved binge-watching in eight-hour chunks. While his castmates and colleagues praised the show's consistently high level of writing, its undying underdog optimism and the genuine warmth of the Belcher family dynamic, Benjamin went in a different direction when describing what made Bob's Burgers such an enduring hit – “It's a soporific, I've heard it puts people to sleep,” he said. "Everyone needs to sleep!" Kristen Schaal agreed. Advertisement Eugene Mirman chimed in, "It's the world's funniest Xanax!" Although Benjamin and his colleagues were joking around when they suggested Bob's Burgers as an over-the-internet alternative to insomnia medication, they may be on to something – a cursory Google search brings up dozens of YouTube videos designed to use the sound of Bob's Burgers episodes to induce sleep in viewers. There is also a small-but-mighty Reddit community dedicated to the practice of using Bob's Burgers P.M. to treat insomnia, sporting the cheeky title /r/SleepingWithBob . In the main Bob's Burgers subreddit, there's even a popular thread dedicated to picking the perfect Bob's Burgers episode for falling asleep, with early season bangers like "Broadcast Wagstaff School News," "My Big Fat Greek Bob" and the entirety of Season Two leading the pack. Benjamin may not have been serious about Bob's Burgers being popular for its sleep-inducing properties – and, to be fair, the community of Bob's Burgers sleepers doesn't seem to be quite large enough to keep the ratings at uncancelable levels for sixteen seasons – but there really is something about the show that gets the restless sleepers of the fandom comfortable. Hopefully Bob's Burgers isn't causing anyone to sleepwalk – this time of year is a dangerous one for turkeys in the toilet. Vanessa Hudgens is taking her fans along on her pregnancy journey. The High School Musical alum —who’s expecting her second child with husband Cole Tucker —showed her followers how big her baby bump is getting as she posed in a sheer chainmail crop on Monday. In a photo shot by photographer Emilynn Rose , Hudgens’s bare baby bump was set against the backdrop of Los Angeles’s skyline as she soaked up some sun on a balcony lined with sheets of clear glass. Leaving her belly exposed, the textured metallic bra top contrasted against her rule-breaking white skirt, which was trimmed with a white lace accent along its low-rise waistband and featured a flowing silhouette with its delicate material. text: Zac Efron fans left in disbelief after his 'REAL singing voice' exposed in leaked High School Musical clip | Daily Mail Online Home Showbiz TV News Lifestyle Sports Health Science Royals Money Real Estate Media U.K. Video Buyline Fashion Beauty Food & Drink Fitness & Wellbeing Love & Sex Family & Parenting Homes Horoscopes My Profile Logout Login US Edition Privacy Policy Feedback Thursday, Nov 27th 2025 4AM 55°F 7AM 52°F 5-Day Forecast Advertisement Zac Efron fans left in disbelief after his 'REAL singing voice' exposed in leaked High School Musical clip A video claiming to show Efron's real singing voice was shared online High School Musical fans are in disbelief after hearing his 'pitchy' performance More, Disney 'planning another woke live-action remake' of animated classic By EMILY LEFROY, US CHIEF LIFESTYLE REPORTER Published: 15:15 EST, 12 November 2025 | Updated: 15:24 EST, 12 November 2025 e-mail 35 shares 12 View comments Get'cha... voice in the game? Almost 20 years after Zac Efron played Troy Bolton in High School Musical, longtime fans are in shock over what his actual singing voice sounded like - and they don't love what they are hearing. While Efron, now 38, played the basketball-player-turned-singer in the Disney franchise, Canadian actor and singer Drew Seeley provided the character's vocals for the first film. Efron, who gained international recognition for the leading role, did not sing in the first film but his real voice was used in the second and third movies. In a clip which has been shared on social media, Efron is seen in a basketball scene singing Get'cha Head in the Game. The video claims to be a leaked tape from the first film, with the 17 Again actor hitting a particularly pitchy part during the crescendo of the song. While most fans commented it wasn't a 'terrible' performance overall, they agreed Seeley's voice was better suited to the songs. 'While it is just a demo, he's very vocally weak. I think what they did for the movie was the best choice,' one shared. Zac Efron shot to fame in High School Musical, which premiered on the Disney Channel in 2006 Efron, pictured in 2024, has sung in several movies since including The Greatest Showman and Hairspray 'Thank God they didn't choose these vocals, but he got a lot better tho eventually,' one penned. 'Disney Channel said, "at the end of the day, this is a BUSINESS." And they did the absolute right thing with having Drew sing!' one person commented. 'The movie would have been dragged if they kept Zac's original vocals (which aren't terrible, but can not lead off a franchise musical film).' 'Do not come for my man Zac. The people need to know why. Kenny Ortega himself saying Zac had a lovely voice but the songs were written before he was initially cast,' defended another. 'Zac is genuinely so lucky he could act well enough that they waited for him to step his vocal cookies up for the second movie… because this was simply not gonna work,' a third said. Efron's real vocals have been used in several other films, including Hairspray and The Greatest Showman. In 2024, during an interview with Entertainment Tonight , director Kenny Ortega explained they used a blend of Efron and Seeley's voices in the first film. 'The songs were written before Zac got the role,' he shared. 'So although he could sing, and he had a lovely voice, it wasn't the voice that the songs were written for.' Seeley, now 43, has since spoken out about the performance. Seeley, who also auditioned for the role, said Zac was the right man to play Troy - especially due to his chemistry with his on-screen love interest, Vanessa Hudgens. Fans were shocked to hear Efron's real singing voice in the first film of the franchise, many admitting the decision to use a different singer's vocals was the right one Drew Seeley provided the vocals for Efron's characters in the first High School Musical film 'I was a good five, six years older than Vanessa,' he told E! News in 2024. 'So in my mind, that had something to do with it. I probably didn't look right with the lineup of everybody else. He co-wrote Get'cha Head in the Game with composers Ray Cham and Greg Cham before also playing Troy Bolton in the High School Musical stage tour. 'Also, Zac is a very talented actor and was great in the role. So, I think they did it right,' he added. Seeley said he has met Efron 'a few times' since providing vocals for him almost 20 years ago. 'But I spent, by far, the least amount of time with Zac compared to any other cast member in High School Musical because I was really only brought in when he was unavailable or not around,' he explained. Seeley admitted that they made the right decision to cast Efron, saying he was more age-appropriate to play Vanessa Hudgens' love interest (Pictured: Efron and Hudgens) Original demo of "Get'cha Head in the Game" with the vocals of Zac Efron leak online. 20 years after the release we can finally hear his voice. With the date from June 2005 the song has some different adlibs and the instrumental was still under production. #HSM20 pic.twitter.com/Tfa2vlVM4P — High School Musical Fan Archive (@archive_hsm) November 11, 2025 High School Musical was released on the Disney channel in 2006 when Efron was 19 years old. The film also starred Vanessa Hudgens, Ashley Tisdale, Corbin Bleu, Lucas Grabeel and Monique Coleman. Last year, Efron re-watched the famous dance i n a Scene Selection segment for Vanity Fair. As his character moved around the basketball court singing and dancing, Efron held up the remote to his face and was unable to stop grinning. He began to rhythmically move to the tune and began laughing when the scene was put on pause amidst the interview. 'First thing that comes to mind is that I really drilled all those shots,' he recalled. 'There's no CGI in there. I don't think we had the budget for that,' he explained. 'So, that makes me feel good.' 'That just takes me back to where all of us were at. All the young men on that team, we were so young and so incredibly motivated.' A newly surfaced clip on social media claims to reveal Efron’s original demo vocals for High School Musical ’s Get’cha Head in the Game , and fans can’t stop reacting. The short video, posted Tuesday, features the actor performing the song during the movie’s famous basketball scene. The post reads, “20 years after the release we can finally hear his voice. With the date from June 2005 the song has some different adlibs and the instrumental was still under production.” While Efron played basketball star Troy Bolton in the 2006 Disney Channel hit, the vocals used in the film were actually recorded by actor and singer Drew Seeley. The demo appears to show what Efron’s voice sounded like before that switch, and the reactions online have been mixed. “Okay this isn’t the worst but it shows how much he really improved in the later films,” one fan commented, adding that Efron “lowkey owes Drew Seeley for this starting point in his career.” Others were more direct, with one writing, “This sounds a mess,” and another exclaiming, “Thank god for Drew Seeley cause omfg my ears!!!!!! They bleeding!!!!” Some even pointed out that the leaked clip makes it clear why Seeley’s vocals were chosen. “No way, that’s why they gave the job to Drew Seeley,” one fan wrote. Efron went on to record his own songs for High School Musical 2 (2007) and High School Musical 3: Senior Year (2008), as well as in the hit musical film Hairspray . Drew Seeley, who originally auditioned for the role of Troy, later told E! News that there were no hard feelings, explaining that Efron was “better suited” for the part because of his chemistry with Vanessa Hudgens. Director Kenny Ortega also shed light on the decision, revealing to Entertainment Tonight that “the songs were written before Zac got the role.” Ortega said that while Efron “had a lovely voice,” it didn’t fit what the songs required at the time. “So he sang everything, and then we dubbed parts of it so that it had greater vocal strength,” Ortega explained. “But the second movie and the third movie, everything was written for him. And that’s important for people to know, that Zac Efron did sing.” Now, nearly two decades later, fans are hearing that early version for the first time, and whether they love it or not, it’s a fascinating glimpse into how far Efron’s voice, and career, have come since High School Musical first aired. He is also an experienced baseball writer with over six years of articles between multiple outlets, most notably FanSided's CubbiesCrib . Whether it's taking in a baseball game, a new season of Futurama or Castlevania: Nocturne , or playing the latest From Software title, he is always finding ways to show his fandom. When it comes to gaming and anything that takes inspiration from it, he is deeply opinionated on what's going on. Outside of entertainment, he's a graduate of Eureka College with a Bachelor's in Communication where he honed his craft as a writer. Between The IV Leader at Illinois Valley Community College and The Pegasus at Eureka, he spent the majority of his college career publishing articles on everything from politics to campus happenings and, of course, entertainment for the student body. Those principles he learned covering the 2020 election, Palestine, and so much more are brought here to Collider, where he has gleefully written on everything from the SAG-AFTRA and WGA strikes to Nathan Lane baby-birding sewer boys. Instead of a divorcee attempting to win his kids back by disguising himself as a matronly, caring nanny in the Robin Williams classic , however, this feature casts Alexandra Breckenridge as a single mom seeking extra cash by disguising herself as the perfect St. Nick for a luxury ski resort. We're excited to bring a new look at the unconventional blend of ideas to Collider's Exclusive Preview event for upcoming winter film and television releases, though it doesn't spotlight the faux Claus. Instead, it shows Breckenridge's love interest, played by Cross 's Ryan Eggold , alongside Sister, Sister star Tia Mowry , who'll put her plans in jeopardy. Our still finds Matthew (Eggold) and Natascha (Mowry) coupled up just outside the resort and looking a bit romantic themselves . Like Breckenridge's scheming Taylor, Natascha will be in close proximity to the Sun Peaks manager throughout the film, as the trailer shows she'll be digging into the origins of their mystery Santa once Taylor starts raising suspicion. If she also has an interest in Matthew, she might just thwart Taylor in more ways than one. Regardless of whether sparks begin flying for them or not, her presence is more than enough to raise the stakes of the mom's humorous holiday hoax . My Secret Santa follows Taylor as she tries desperately to find a way to pay for her daughter's acceptance into the elite snowboarding camp at the Sun Peaks resort. With the help of some loved ones, she undergoes a transformation into a rosy-cheeked older gentleman with a big white beard to rival the real St Nick . "Hugh Mann" quickly lands a gig as the resort's Santa and becomes a sensation despite some near-misses. It's all going better than Taylor could've imagined, until she starts falling for Matthew , the man she once rejected and now spends time with in her working hours. Complications from their chemistry threaten to upend her entire Santa scheme and a prospective relationship. Rounding out this Christmas tale are Madison MacIsaac and Diana Maria Riva . 'My Secret Santa' Director Is a Netflix Holiday Romance Favorite my-secret-santa-netflix Adding to the excitement for My Secret Santa is the man behind the camera — Mike Rohl . He's responsible for masterminding one of Netflix's defining Christmas romance trilogies in The Princess Switch , starring Vanessa Hudgens as both a Chicago baker and a duchess who swap lives around the holidays and end up forever intertwined. In more recent years, he's continued the trend of making seasonal love stories , like Bringing Christmas Home and Hallmark's Falling Together . Joining him on his latest holiday venture are writers Carley Smale and Ron Oliver and producers Howard and Alexander Braunstein . My Secret Santa comes down the chimney onto Netflix on December 3. (Image credit: Getty Images) By Ariel Baker published 31 October 2025 in News Khloé Kardashian is a long-time nail aficionado, and I don’t think she gets the credit that she deserves. On October 30, the reality TV star shared a video of her latest manicure on Instagram, and like a moth to a flame, I couldn’t look away. The look was a perfect mix of glam and drama, yet still practical, thanks to the simple yet elegant finish she chose. To start, extensions were applied to Kardashian’s nails for extra length. They were then cut and filed into an almond shape before being painted a glittery silver. A magnet was then used to bring out the real star of the show, the cat eye effect that made it look like they came to life under different types of lighting. The gorgeous color felt glam enough to catch eyes and spark conversation, yet was subtle enough for me to consider it a serious contender for a 2025 holiday manicure. Khloe Kardashian showing her silver cat eye nails. (Image credit: Getty Images) Cat eye polishes are the perfect manicure for those who want their nails to look a little more glam, without spending too much extra time at the nail salon. The magic of this look lies in the polish itself, allowing you to achieve a highly detailed manicure without worrying about nail charms falling off, snagging, or matching the designs on your fingers with your outfit. Not only is silver practically a neutral, but the suspended glitter in the polish also adds an expensive feel to the look. Share Article Share Article Facebook X LinkedIn Reddit Bluesky Email Copy Link Link copied Bookmark Comments By Molly Toolan 12:51, Sun, Nov 2, 2025 Updated: 12:51, Sun, Nov 2, 2025 The film was released in 2022 (Image: Netflix) For lovers of animation and rom-coms , Netflix has you covered. The streaming platform is home to an "amazing" film that has become a favourite of viewers. Entergalactic was released in 2022 and is an adult animated film special created by American musician and actor Kid Cudi. The movie serves as a visual companion piece to Cudi's album of the same name. The film premiered exclusively on Netflix , simultaneously with the album's release. Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT Directed by Fletcher Moules, it is based on the record, which Cudi recorded before storyboarding the movie. Alongside Cudi, it stars the voices of Jessica Williams, Timothée Chalamet, Ty Dolla Sign, Laura Harrier, Vanessa Hudgens, Christopher Abbott, 070 Shake, Teyana Taylor, Jaden Smith, Keith David, Arturo Castro, and Macaulay Culkin. The romantic comedy uses an art style inspired by that of I Lost My Body (2019) and When Harry Met Sally... (1989). This may include adverts from us and 3rd parties based on our understanding. You can unsubscribe at any time. Read our Privacy Policy The film's synopsis reads: "Ambitious artist Jabari attempts to balance success and love when he moves into his dream Manhattan apartment and falls for his next-door neighbour." Entergalactic received critical acclaim for its animation, visual style, music, and story. It is dedicated to Cudi's deceased friend, American fashion designer Virgil Abloh, who served as a costume designer on the project before his death. Alongside this, the release date coincides with Abloh's birth date. Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT The film has an impressive 97% rating on Rotten Tomatoes, with one describing it as a "masterpiece". Article continues below ADVERTISEMENT They added: "This movie was a masterpiece. The emotions in this movie felt real. It felt relatable, and the music in the movie only made what felt real feel realer if that makes sense. I wish to see more movies like this, but in the meantime, I will watch this movie a hundred times more." Entergalactic is available to stream on Netflix right now (Image: Netflix) Another viewer said: "The most beautiful animation I have seen in a movie I wasn't expecting much going into this movie, and the only reason I really watched it was because of Kid Cudi, but I was pleasantly surprised. The animation is pure perfection, and don't get me started on the transitions. It got some laughs out of me, and I never checked how much time was left throughout the movie. It's a solid story that I would probably recommend to my friend. One of my favourite aspects was Mr Rager. Now, when I say this, I mean like when his shadow is replaced by him or when he gives him advice on DMing his ex. Overall all I really enjoyed Entergalactic, five stars." "One of my FAVOURITE MOVIES! I love this movie, the soundtrack to this movie is also so great," added a third. Entergalactic is available to stream on Netflix right now. Have you seen stories about ' Chucky ,' 'Scream,' ' Buffy the Vampire Slayer ,' 'The Boys,' 'Vanderpump Rules,' or any of ' The Real Housewives ' franchises? That's probably a Britta DeVore-curated piece of art, and it sounds like you have great taste. When she isn't sitting behind her laptop bringing readers her hot takes on upcoming projects or keeping the dream alive in the Senior News team, Britta can usually be found outside hiking or inside behind her drum set. She also has a tiny cat named Athena that she loves more than anything else in the world and is always happy for new brewery recs. Sign in to your Collider account follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread 5 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Apple TV has struck gold in the Alaskan wilderness. With new episodes of staple hits like Slow Horses and The Morning Show rolling out week after week, one would think there would be an all-out war for the top spot on the streamer’s global Top 10. Alas, there is but one title that has sat at the top of the chart since its grand debut aired earlier this month. That would be the Jason Clarke -led action-centered crime thriller, The Last Frontier . In the days since the network’s original series burst onto screens on October 10, audiences around the world have faithfully tuned in to watch the pulse-pounding action and high-stakes drama play out, helping it carve out the number one spot and not let go. Although no Season 2 renewal has been announced at this time, it seems more than likely that the platform will want to push through with more where that came from, considering the show’s global takeover. For those unfamiliar, The Last Frontier channels the things viewers love about shows like Yellowstone and Jack Ryan, then flips them on their head before dropping the main characters into the Alaskan wilderness. Starring Clarke as a US Marshal named Frank Remnick, the story follows a flight filled with some of the country’s most dangerous prisoners after it crashes just outside of Fairbanks, Alaska. With high-risk fugitives now on the loose, Frank has his hands full protecting his beloved town and those closest to him. Meanwhile, the CIA soon gets involved when they discover that one of the runaway convicts is a man they’ve been trying to detain for quite some time. Meet the Team Behind ‘The Last Frontier’ The parallels between The Last Frontier and other hit shows of today or yesteryear aren’t completely hard to understand when you learn that the man behind the series is none other than Jon Bokenkamp . Although he’s been involved in a multitude of other successful small-screen productions, Bokenkamp is best known as the creator behind the 10-season-running James Spader -led crime thriller, The Blacklist . Meanwhile, many of the gorgeous shots that have sucked audiences into The Last Frontier were all under the vision of its frequent director, Sam Hargrave , who fans will know from Netflix’s Extraction film franchise. In addition to Clarke’s leading role as the rough and tough US Marshal, The Last Frontier also features dynamite performances from an impressive ensemble that features the talents of Dallas Goldtooth ( Fallout ), Dominic Cooper ( Mamma Mia ), Simone Kessell ( Yellowjackets ), Haley Bennett ( The Girl on the Train ), Alfre Woodard ( Star Trek: First Contact ) and Tait Blum ( For All Mankind ). Sign in to your Collider account follow Follow followed Followed Like Like Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap True Detective returned for a successful fourth season seven years after Season 3 aired. Subtitled "Night Country," the season was largely a hit due to its Alaska setting. Apple TV has released another show with a similar setting , and it is dominating the streamer's top ten chart. The Last Frontier has been airing for five weeks and is currently at the top of the chart, according to current data from FlixPatrol. It has dethroned fan-favorite dramas like The Morning Show and Slow Horses , which are also releasing new episodes weekly. Set in one of the coldest places on Earth, The Last Frontier is a crime thriller created by The Blacklist creator Jon Bokenkamp . Unlike True Detective , which explores crime with some supernatural undertones, The Last Frontier grounds its premise in government conspiracies. At the center of it all is U.S. Marshal Frank Remnick ( Jason Clarke ), who is tasked with overseeing law and order in his remote, tight-knit community. However, things take a turn when a prisoner transport airplane crashes on the tundra. The show's official logline explains: "Remnick's jurisdiction is turned upside down when a prison transport plane crashes in the remote wilderness, setting free dozens of violent inmates. Tasked with protecting the town he’s vowed to keep safe, he begins to suspect the crash wasn’t an accident, but the first step of a well-crafted plan with far-reaching and devastating implications." The Last Frontier features Bokenkamp's signature themes, including criminal masterminds, government conspiracies, and complex federal officers. Bokenkamp wrote the show alongside Richard D'Ovidio . Other cast members include Dominic Cooper (Havlock), Haley Bennett (Sidney), Simone Kessell (Sarah), Dallas Goldtooth (Hutch), Tait Blum (Luke), and Alfre Woodard (Bradford). What's Going On With 'True Detective' Season 5? Since HBO renewed the show for a fifth season following the success of Season 4, updates have been rolling in, with writer-showrunner Issa López landing in Jamaica Bay, New York, as her next location. Nicolas Cage is in talks to lead the season, whose details are being kept under wraps. "Issa has a lot to say, not unlike she did with Night Country . It’s a different milieu but just as powerful," HBO's Head of Drama Series and Film, Francesca Orsi , said in an interview. Production is set to start imminently, with a targeted 2027 launch date . In the meantime, new episodes of The Last Frontier are available to stream on Fridays on Apple TV. The logline for this week's episode reads: "Fairbanks is hit with a mass power outage. Sarah spots someone suspicious in the ER. Sidney tries to get control of a key piece of evidence." To note just a few – Cleopatra, Queen Elizabeth I, Madame Curie, Amelia Earhart, etc… Let’s add one more, much less known for her exploits than for her world-renowned champagne, Veuve Clicquot. This film brings the 27 year-old widow Barbe-Nicole Ponsardin Clicquot (Haley Bennett) to the forefront in a beautifully recounted tale of her tumultuous marriage to François (Tom Sturbridge), the young owner of the Clicquot family champagne company. It is the early 1800s, they are madly in love, he conveys to her his passion for the champagne vines and trade, and she is an ardent, talented pupil. After his suicide, as inheritor, she insists on continuing the Clicquot line, declining to sell to vulture-like competitors such as a Monsieur Moët, despite financial and family worries. The Napoleonic wars and the ensuing trade edicts create further problems for her, but she does not cave in to the many pressures around her. This is a surprisingly entertaining and revealing biopic about someone many of us never knew existed. And it’s quite ironic that such a French tale should be told by the British – produced by Joe Wright, with Thomas Napper as director and a full English cast. Chapeau ! NOW YOU SEE ME, NOW YOU DON’T 3 (INSAISISSABLES 3) *1/2 No, number 3 is not a charm. With all the hocus pocus, card tricks and (supposed) suspense, it’s still a dud and predictable, like the first two. They keep churning them out. Seriously? Do they even make money? However, Roxanne is also a woman Cyrano loves, leading to an awkward love triangle. ‌ Believing his appearance makes him unworthy of her, Cyrano agrees to write romantic letters for Christian to give to Roxanne, in the hope of winning her love. The plot revolves around a love triangle, where Roxanne falls for the words but not the man, resulting in dramatic and emotional consequences and a dramatic fallout. READ MORE : 'Disturbing' horror film is 'frighteningly real' and on ITV tonight READ MORE : 'Finest war film ever made' with Hollywood icons airing today on BBC The movie was released in 2021 and features stunning footage from being filmed on location in Sicily. After its release, it was nominated for awards including Golden Globes, BAFTAs, and an Oscar for Best Costume Design. Despite critical acclaim, Cyrano was considered a box office disappointment, grossing only $6.4million against a $30m budget. The film has also been well-received by fans, who shared their thoughts in reviews on the film ratings website Rotten Tomatoes. One person wrote: "One of my favourites, it’s sincere, sad, fun, love it." Another posted: "Excellent acting and wonderful music." ‌ A third posted, "I am a romantic and I LOVE this film. "Absolutely blew me away. This is brilliant. One of the best movies I've ever seen," said another. Many praised Game of Thrones star Drinklage for his lead role in this, as one person wrote, "This is truly a beautiful film. The music supports the dialogue well, and the filming was exquisite. ‌ "Peter Dinklage was the best in this. He has a lovely, expressive face, and his emotions appeared truly genuine. Anyone would fall in love with him. Well done, we all really enjoyed this." "This is Peter Dinklage's greatest performance. The story is romantic and moving, and the emotion displayed by Dinklage feels realistic and impactful," claimed another viewer. However, not everyone is a fan, with some pointing out their love for Drinklage but found the film missed the mark due to changes to the original plot. Article continues below One person gave it just one star as they wrote: "I didn’t like it. Why do all these remakes have to make major changes to the story. By Karen Butler 1 of 4 | Haley Bennett and Dominic Cooper star in "The Last Frontier." New episodes stream on Fridays. Photo courtesy of Apple TV. NEW YORK, Oct. 31 (UPI) -- Preacher, Captain America and Mamma Mia! alum Dominic Cooper says his new TV series, The Last Frontier , is compelling entertainment that also explores important themes like truth and morality. "It was a nonstop page turner," Cooper, 47, told UPI in a recent Zoom interview. "Jon Bokenkamp, our show-runner, refers to it as a cheeseburger, which I didn't understand at first. But I think what he means is there's something for everyone and it felt like, and he's described it, a 1990s[-style] blockbuster action piece, but, at the same time, it's complex," Cooper said. "People are desperately needing to follow a complex story-line about issues that are important and reveal truths and lies about the society in which we live." Airing Fridays on Apple TV, the series casts Jason Clarke as Frank, a U.S. Marshal whose quiet life in Alaska is upended when a plane filled with dangerous criminals -- including Cooper's former CIA asset Havlock -- crashes into the snowy mountains under his jurisdiction. Haley Bennett plays Sidney, a CIA agent sent to re-capture Havlock, her husband, while Simone Kessell plays Sarah, a nurse and Frank's wife. The cast also includes Alfre Woodard and Dallas Goldtooth. Magnificent Seven and Hillbilly Elegy actress Bennett, 37, called the show an "epic" story that also depicts intimate interpersonal relationships. "What drew me in about the project was the humanity and the survival and truth and how people hold on to their values when everything is falling apart and what the truth is really changes and transforms over the 10 episodes," she said. "What I love about The Last Frontier is that it feels familiar in all of the best ways and it kind of turns the genre on its head. It's familiar, but it's unexpected and fresh." Cooper added: "Sometimes when you do the complex pieces with great dialogue and really challenging roles with other actors, you go, 'Oh, I really miss doing action.' And then sometimes when you're doing action, you go, 'I just need something more complex.' "This had everything, so I couldn't complain," Cooper laughed. "There's also sex. There's relationships within this nightmare world, which a lot of people have to live in, survival and dealing with the integrity of a country, the diplomacy of a country. At the same time, they're real people. They have to live normal lives, as well. They exist, these people, and I don't know how they do it." Bennett noted that there are big differences between the Alaskans, the plane crash survivors who terrorize them and the shadowy government agents who seem to know more about the whole situation than they are letting on. "There's such a contrast between the community in which Frank is living in, where everybody takes care of each other, and then the world in which they live in, where it's every man for himself," she said. "On a deeper level, beyond the action, what this is a commentary of is, what we are all doing here, what we're all doing and how we get ourselves into morally ambiguous situations." "This is what I've struggled with daily," Cooper agreed. "It's every man for himself now and morals are at an all-time low. People don't know what their moral compass is. We allow politicians to lie now. You can lie. It's official. You're allowed to talk absolute garbage straight-up," he added. "There's no such thing as facts any more." Bennett said she hopes these themes resonate with audiences. " Last Frontier isn't about survival in the wild. It's about emotional survival and what it costs to hold on to your truth," she added. Digital Journal WORLD TECH & SCIENCE SOCIAL MEDIA BUSINESS ENTERTAINMENT LIFE SPORTS Entertainment Tait Blum talks about starring in ‘The Last Frontier’ on Apple TV Young actor Tait Blum chatted about starring in the series “The Last Frontier” on Apple TV. By Markos Papadatos Published November 11, 2025 Tait Blum in 'The Last Frontier.' Photo Courtesy of Apple TV. Tait Blum in 'The Last Frontier.' Photo Courtesy of Apple TV. Young actor Tait Blum chatted about starring in the series “The Last Frontier” on Apple TV. Blum stars alongside Jason Clarke, Dominic Cooper, Haley Bennett, Simone Kessell, and Alfre Woodard. Margaret Mead once said: “Never doubt that a small group of thoughtful, committed citizens can change the world; indeed, it’s the only thing that ever has.” This quote applies to Tait Blum, who is a revelation in “The Last Frontier.” Experience making ‘The Last Frontier’ “The Last Frontier” follows Frank Remnick (Jason Clarke), the lone U.S. marshal in charge of the quiet, rugged barrens of Alaska. Remnick’s jurisdiction is turned upside down when a prison transport plane crashes in the remote wilderness, setting free dozens of violent inmates. Tasked with protecting the town he’s vowed to keep safe, he begins to suspect the crash wasn’t an accident, but the first step of a well-crafted plan with far-reaching and devastating implications. On his experience making “The Last Frontier,” he remarked, “It has been amazing! It has been quite a wild ride like the show.” Playing Luke, the son of Jason Clarke’s character On playing Luke, the son of Jason Clarke’s character, he said, “Jason is amazing! He has been doing this for so many years, and he is such a veteran.” “I really loved picking his brain and being on set with him,” he admitted. “Jason is absolutely incredible! I think we look quite a bit alike too, so that’s nice. Our resemblance is almost uncanny.” Lessons learned from this screenplay On the lessons learned from this screenplay, Blum reflected, “It taught me that Luke is such a very brave character, and he is someone who values family so much. Luke is also a loyal character. I realize that through Luke especially that I understand a lot of things about myself.” “I’m very loyal and I would perhaps have reacted the same way and he did because I care about my family so deeply,” Blum noted. “This show brought me together with my family, and I feel that it’s a lesson in loyalty,” he acknowledged. The digital age On being a part of the digital age, Blum said, “I think it’s interesting! I guess I am one of the last generations in the fully digital age.” “It can be a bit overwhelming at times; I have to get away, but I think it’s quite cool,” he added. Advice for young and emerging actors For young and aspiring actors, Blum said, “Rejection is not a bad thing. The more rejections you can take, the better you can handle that, and the better you’re going to be in the long run.” “Grit is so important,” he underscored. “So, just keep pushing forward and continue to do the work; that’s so valuable.” Future plans Regarding his future plans, he shared, “I love making films and doing television so much, and I am just going to keep going whatever comes my way.” “I’ll do whatever project I wind up loving in the same way that I loved this show. I think I’m going to see where the wind takes me, and I will continue to look for character-driven projects like this one,” he explained. Stage of his life On the title of the current chapter of his life, Blum revealed, “A New Beginning.” Superpower of choice Blum’s superpower of choice would be “flight.” “It would be so cool to fly,” he admitted. “I would be able to take off and go wherever I want without having to pay for a ticket.” Success On his definition of the word success, he expressed, “Being able to look back in 40 years and say that ‘I’ve told the stories that I want to tell,’ and that my family is completely taken care of. Also, the peace of mind that comes with that.” Message to his fans For his fans and supporters, Blum said, “First and foremost, I want to say that I love them! My fans are very loyal. I’m super excited to bring them more things to look forward to and to watch.” Closing thoughts on ‘The Last Frontier’ “I just want the fans to have a really good time,” he exclaimed about “The Last Frontier.” “I think that ‘The Last Frontier’ is such an entertaining and explosive show. It’s a fun, vibrant project and I want them to be able to sit back and enjoy it,” Blum concluded. To learn more about actor Tait Blum, follow him on Instagram , and check out his IMDb page . All Rights Reserved Actors Who Received Oscar And Razzie Nominations For The Same Role NEWS MOVIES TV TRAILERS REVIEWS EXCLUSIVES FEATURES Newsletter Movies Comedy Movies Actors Who Received Oscar And Razzie Nominations For The Same Role By Nina Starner Nov. 3, 2025 10:00 am EST Netflix Ask any actor at basically any level of fame and notoriety and they'll probably tell you that they dream of winning an Academy Award for one of their performances. The award, also called the Oscar, has been around since 1929 and is given, each year, to the best cinematic achievements and performances. (Well, that's the idea , but sometimes, performances and movies win Oscars that perhaps should have gone to other nominees , which is its own thing entirely.) Whether you're just nominated or you take home the gold during the ceremony, "Oscar nominee" and "Oscar winner" get permanently tacked onto your name forever. It is, I can only imagine, incredibly special! Now imagine that you're an actor and you get a call from your team telling you that you've been nominated for an Academy Award, you've also been nominated for a Golden Raspberry Award. On the complete other side of the spectrum, a Golden Raspberry, usually just referred to as a Razzie, cheekily honors the absolute worst movies and performances every year; after the first "ceremony" was held in 1981 in the living room of founder John J. B. Wilson, they've become a strange sort of industry staple, offering up dubious "awards" for actors and directors. (They don't give Razzies for production aspects, which is good, actually.) As of this writing, only one actor has won an Oscar and a Razzie in the very same year — Sandra Bullock for "The Blind Side" and "All About Steve" — but a handful of others have received nominations for both "awards" for the exact same role , which is potentially even more impressive (in a weird way). So who are they, and what are the roles? James Coco, Only When I Laugh Columbia Pictures Directed by Glenn Jordan and penned by acclaimed screenwriter and playwright Neil Simon, "Only When I Laugh" — which is actually adapted from Simon's play "The Gingerbread Lady" — centers around struggling actress Georgia Hines (Marsha Mason), who returns to New York after a prolonged stay at a facility to try and overcome her alcohol addiction. Upon her arrival, she reunites with her two best friends: socialite Toby Landau (Joan Hackett, who earned a best supporting actress nomination at the Oscars) and similarly struggling actor Jimmy Perrino (James Coco). Coco is, of course, the person in this project with the distinction of earning an Oscar and a Razzie nod for the same role. As Georgia tries to adapt to her sobriety — amidst some drama with her ex David Lowe (David Dukes) and as she tries to be a good mother to her daughter Polly (Kristy McNichol) — we also watch Coco's Jimmy go through a pretty rough journey, finally booking a big role in a play before getting fired only a few days before the first performance. (Also, weirdly, Kevin Bacon plays a bit part in this movie!) Both the Razzies and the Oscars took notice of Coco's role as Jimmy, and the rest is history. Coco lost the Oscar to legendary British actor John Gielgud, who took home the award for his role as Hobson in Steve Gordon's romantic comedy "Arthur" — and the Razzie for which he was nominated went to Steve Forrest, who played Greg Savitt in the infamously campy drama "Mommie Dearest." Amy Irving, Yentl MGM/UA Entertainment Company Barbra Streisand may have won a Golden Globe for her directorial feature debut "Yentl" in 1981 — a film which also features her as its titular character, a young Ashkenazi Jewish woman living in a Polish shtetl who steadfastly refuses to get married — but her co-star Amy Irving got all of the attention from awards ceremonies in both good and bad ways. After Yentl's father — who was secretly helping her study the Talmud even though women are forbidden from doing such things — passes away, she cuts her hair and poses as a boy named Anshel, the name of her brother who also passed. This is where things get tricky, though ... because Yentl is so good at pretending to be a young man that, when she enrolls in a Jewish school known as Yeshiva, a fellow student's fiancée, Hadass Vishtower (Irving), starts falling in love with her. Not only that, but after Hadass' engagement to that student, Avigdor (Mandy Patinkin), is called off, Hadass and "Anshel" end up married, though they obvious can't consummate the union in the way that Hadass probably expected. As Hadass falls for Yentl as Anshel, Yentl is herself falling in love with Avigdor, and after he's sent away from the Yeshiva, the two end up finding each other despite both of their previous commitments to Hadass. So what competition did Irving face for her role as Hadass at both ceremonies? Irving lost her Razzie to Sybil Danning, who, somewhat astoundingly, won it for two projects — the exploitation film "Chained Heat" and Lou Ferrigno's take on "Hercules" — and lost her Academy Award to Linda Hunt for her role as Billy Kwan in Peter Weir's film "The Year of Living Dangerously." Glenn Close, Hillbilly Elegy Netflix In 2016, James Donald Bowman, who was then going by JD Vance, wrote a memoir called "Hillbilly Elegy," and in 2020, Ron Howard's adaptation of the book hit Netflix. Despite blowback over the book and debates about whether or not Vance was fair or even accurate about his suburban Ohio origins — because the book paints a rather dire picture of his upbringing — the movie brought in an all-star cast, including Amy Adams as Vance's mother Beverly, Freida Pinto as his eventual wife Usha, Haley Bennett as his older sister Lindsay, and Glenn Close as his well-meaning but rough grandmother Mamaw. If they want to speak [French], they can, if they want to ignore papa, they can.” Over the past 30-plus years, Clarke has done it all on screen. Oscar nominees and winners? Yeah, he’s starred in those, too: Oppenheimer and First Man , to name two. Advertisement It’s an almost perfect career trajectory, good work without the fuss – most stories about Clarke all feature the same line, that he’s happy not being famous, that it’s all about the work – and that is all true. He is one of those classic character actors that cause people to go, “Oh, him”, and while in The Sydney Morning Herald office last week, he caused a few quizzical double-takes of the “Where do I know him from?” variety. Loading Being back in Australia has caused a bit of a head spin. He remembers being a young actor and sitting on a bench at Milson’s Point, outside a casting office, nervously going over his lines. He remembers being cast in the TV movie, BlackJack, with Colin Friels, where Clarke turned up to set with his tie undone. “And the director just f---ing gave it to me, ‘You come to set ready.’ And that’s always stayed with me – you come to set ready.” He currently has three high-profile projects across three different streamers – The Last Frontier on Apple TV, the film, A House of Dynamite, on Netflix and the true-crime series, Murdaugh: Death in the Family , on Disney+. Each role requires something different from him: physicality in Frontier , a cool demeanour in the face of nuclear disaster in Dynamite and a Southern patriarch with a killer instinct in Murdaugh , for which he packed on the weight, ending up at more than 100 kilograms with a substantial belly. Patricia Arquette and Jason Clarke in Murdaugh: Death in the Family. “It is rough,” he says. “And then it’s also like, there you are in Montreal with a plane and a helicopter [for The Last Frontier ], and there you are in Atlanta [for Murdaugh ]. And yes, it is a little uncomfortable. In Atlanta, it was difficult to live with [the weight] for so long and then try and take it off as part of the shoot. You’ve got a funny relationship with food and you end up hating it because you’re gonna force yourself to eat it, then you force yourself not to eat it. You’re getting around just angry.” Is he happy now? Advertisement “I’m OK now, yeah,” he says, laughing. “I’ve still got a couple of kilograms to get back to what I was before I started putting it on. It is enjoyable, but it’s an intense business.” Loading Clarke grew up in South Australia and Queensland. A photo of him from his Townsville high school yearbook lists his interests as AFL (he doesn’t get to see much of it in LA, he says), studying law (which he did before swapping to drama in Sydney and then studying drama again at the Victorian College of the Arts in Melbourne), and “enjoying a good social life and to eventually travel”. “That’s part of the reason I wanted to be an actor,” he says. “To just get out. That was where I thought the point of life was to just go and make the most of this thing you’ve been given. And that’s how I choose my roles, still. It’s a gut thing. Ultimately, it’s ‘do I want to do this?’” The Last Frontier sees Clarke take another step forward in his career: he is not only No.1 on the call sheet as the lead actor, he’s also, for the first time, an executive producer. Kyle Chandler and Jason Clarke in Zero Dark Thirty. “It helped me find the character,” he says. “In a way, Frank [Remnick, his character] is the same thing. It’s up to me to take care of everybody else and to make sure that all my other actors are happy, that the crew is happy, that I’m not taking up all the time on the day, that I’m getting my takes done. Advertisement “I like that responsibility. I did show up every day knowing my stuff, being able to execute it and move on and not drag the chain and find the positives. And it’s a big thing when you’re doing these things for so long because you have to let go of a whole bunch of things. Can we do another 10 takes? Yes. Is it going to get any better? Maybe. But if we have enough to move on, let’s just, let’s keep the ball rolling.” How does he feel things have changed since he started acting, compared with what they are now? The opportunities for actors are huge, but a lot more is also asked of them. “In a way, it hasn’t changed for me,” he says. “The business has changed, but my process is still the same, and it always was. It hasn’t altered what I do. And I’m still a voice, movement, text-based, actor. The press has changed and media has changed. It [your work] goes everywhere now a lot quicker. Theresa Cutknife, Jason Clarke, Haley Bennett, Dallas Goldtooth and Martin Roach in The Last Frontier. “The streamers, they’ve all got this metric and numbers and everything coming in. You listen to that, or you don’t, there’s this feedback, and whether something’s working or not, that’s instantaneous. You’re aware of that. So I’ve made a very conscious decision to stay off social media because there’s only so much noise I can handle. “And it’s the same thing with numbers [viewing figures]. It is what it is, you know. You’re constantly being judged, and it’s a funny relationship that you have with it, and you can’t control it. Sometimes I go back and something, something will hurt and something, something will make you feel good. And you go, ‘Well, does that matter to me? Why do I do this?’” So why does he do it? Advertisement “Because I love it,” he says “I make a living out of it. Don’t, get me wrong, this is a job. And I come from a very working-class background, you know, where you have to put food on the table, the basics of just that. And then there’s also, I do love it … it’s a very obsessive compulsive business, and you just have to learn to control that and turn it on and off as you can, and use it as well when it’s required.” Loading While this does make Clarke sound serious, he’s delightful company. Not too keen on having his photo taken, but a complete softie when talking about his two boys. And while he still retains his Australian accent, despite rarely having cause to use it on screen these days, any notion his is just a regular life evaporates when he casually mentions that Jeremy Strong – yes, Succession’s Jeremy Strong, an old friend of Clarke – introduced him to Bruce Springsteen the other day. Hang on, what? “I knew Jeremy when no one would employ him,” Clarke says. “He had a very small role on Zero Dark Thirty , and then I tried to get him on Chappaquiddick with me, and they wouldn’t. And I said, ‘You guys are missing out. I’m telling you, this guy’s gonna bring it.’ I got Elizabeth Debicki a small role on Everest , and there she is [winning awards for playing Princess Diana on The Crown ]. “I like seeing good people, the whole cream rising to the top thing. That’s what I reflect back on now, that you go, ‘Hang on. I am part of this circus, I’m inside the door’.” So what did he say to Bruce? Advertisement “His music’s just touched me at so many parts of my life,” Clarke says. “And you don’t [want to] overwhelm him. But he knew me. Bruce Springsteen knew me! And you go, ‘Man, I didn’t know …’ He’s just lovely. I thanked him. I really did’.” The Last Frontier is now streaming on Apple TV. Ultimately, it’s ‘do I want to do this?’” The Last Frontier sees Clarke take another step forward in his career: he is not only No. 1 on the call sheet as the lead actor, he’s also, for the first time, an executive producer. Kyle Chandler and Jason Clarke in Zero Dark Thirty. “It helped me find the character,” he says. “In a way, Frank [Remnick, his character] is the same thing. It hasn’t altered what I do. And I’m still a voice, movement, text-based, actor. The press has changed and media has changed. It [your work] goes everywhere now a lot quicker. You listen to that, or you don’t, there’s this feedback, and whether something’s working or not, that’s instantaneous. So I’ve made a very conscious decision to stay off social media because there’s only so much noise I can handle. “And it’s the same thing with numbers [viewing figures]. It is what it is, you know. You’re constantly being judged, and it’s a funny relationship that you have with it, and you can’t control it. Sometimes I go back and something, something will hurt and something, something will make you feel good. And you go, ‘Well, does that matter to me? Why do I do this?’” So why does he do it? “Because I love it,” he says “I make a living out of it. Don’t, get me wrong, this is a job. And I come from a very working-class background, you know, where you have to put food on the table, the basics of just that. And then there’s also, I do love it … it’s a very obsessive compulsive business, and you just have to learn to control that and turn it on and off as you can, and use it as well when it’s required. ” Loading While this does make Clarke sound serious, he’s delightful company. Not too keen on having his photo taken, but a complete softie when talking about his two boys. And while he still retains his Australian accent, despite rarely having cause to use it on screen these days, any notion his is just a regular life evaporates when he casually mentions that Jeremy Strong – yes, Succession’s Jeremy Strong, an old friend of Clarke – introduced him to Bruce Springsteen the other day. Hang on, what? “I knew Jeremy when no one would employ him,” Clarke says. “He had a very small role on Zero Dark Thirty , and then I tried to get him on Chappaquiddick with me, and they wouldn’t. And I said, ‘You guys are missing out. I’m telling you, this guy’s gonna bring it. ’ I got Elizabeth Debicki a small role on Everest , and there she is [winning awards for playing Princess Diana on The Crown ]. “I like seeing good people, the whole cream rising to the top thing. That’s what I reflect back on now, that you go, ‘Hang on. I am part of this circus, I’m inside the door’. ” So what did he say to Bruce? “His music’s just touched me at so many parts of my life,” Clarke says. “And you don’t [want to] overwhelm him. Bruce Springsteen knew me! And you go, ‘Man, I didn’t know …’ He’s just lovely. ” The Last Frontier is now streaming on Apple TV. There’s only one problem: seven “rich pricks” — aka his family — stand between Becket and the big bucks. What is Huntington’s new title? According to a new report from World of Reel, Powell’s latest movie, the revenge thriller Huntingon, is now going by a new name. The film is reportedly now being called How to Make a Killing , and has already seen trailers appear during certain screenings. World of Reel’s report notes that certain showings of The Running Man have already aired the trailer, which dates the film for February 27, 2026. The film, which has been in development since 2024, comes from John Patton Ford, the writer and director of the drama film Emily The Criminal . Early reports on the film note that the original screenplay for the film is inspired by the 1949 Ealing Comedy film Kind Hearts and Coronets, which starred Alec Guinness. Alongside Powell, How to Make a Killing also stars Margaret Qualley, Ed Harris, Jessica Henwick, Zach Woods, Topher Grace, Raff Law, and Bill Camp. Powell has seen a meteoric rise to superstardom following his appearance in 2022’s Top Gun: Maverick. After that role, Powell starred in 2023’s Anyone But You and Hit Man, and then starred in 2024’s Twisters. This year, he led Edgar Wright’s adaptation of The Running Man, and he is also set to star in the upcoming J.J. Abrams film Ghostwriter, which is also set for a 2026 release date. text: Everybody Wants to F--- Me Starring Taron Egerton Gets First Look Skip to content ComingSoon.net - Movie Trailers, TV & Streaming News, and More Open Close Menu Open menu Streaming Schedules Apple TV+ Disney+ Hulu Max Netflix Paramount+ Peacock Prime Video Open menu Movies Movie News Movie Features Movie Reviews Open menu TV TV News TV Features TV Reviews Open menu Games Video Game News Video Game Features Video Game Reviews Trailers Open menu Genres Anime Collectibles Comics Documentaries Family Horror Sci-Fi Wrestling Facebook Instagram Twitter Search Close Search (Photo Credit: Netflix) Movies Everybody Wants to F— Me Starring Taron Egerton Gets First Look November 10, 2025 By Maggie Dela Paz Studiocanal and LuckyChap Entertainment’s upcoming dark comedy thriller Everybody Wants to F— Me has received its first official photo, confirming that production on the Taron Egerton -led movie has finally begun in London. This marks Egerton’s first comedy project since starring in the action thriller Carry-On in 2024 and the crime thriller She Rides Shotgun last August. What does the Everybody Wants to F— Me photo show? The Everybody Wants to F— Me photo features Egerton running in the park with an adorable little dog. In the background, women can be seen diverting all their attention towards him, hinting at the movie’s plot. Further details about the film’s characters and story are still under wraps, but it will reportedly take place in the world of modern dating. Jonathan Schey is directing the comedy thriller movie from a screenplay he also wrote. Besides Egerton, the cast also includes Jessica Henwick (Glass Onion), Mia McKenna-Bruce (The Beatles), Charly Clive, and Herbert Nordrum (The Worst Person in the World). Cecilia Frugiuele and Olivier Kaempfer are producing for Parkville Pictures. It hails from Studiocanal Film4, Parkville Pictures, and LuckyChap, with Studiocanal and Film4 fully financing the project. Ron Halpern, Joe Naftalin, and Isobel Carter are overseeing the movie on behalf of Studiocanal, while Farhana Bhula and David Kimbangi will oversee for Film4. Egerton’s most recent acting credit was the Apple TV crime miniseries Smoke. Besides Everybody Wants to F— Me, he is also currently attached to star opposite Charlize Theron in Netflix’s upcoming action thriller Apex. Besides being a fan of coming-of-age films and shows, she also enjoys watching K-Dramas and listening to her favorite K-Pop groups. Her current TV obsessions right now are FX’s The Bear and the popular anime My Hero Academia. What does the Everybody Wants to F— Me photo show? The Everybody Wants to F— Me photo features Egerton running in the park with an adorable little dog. In the background, women can be seen diverting all their attention towards him, hinting at the movie’s plot. Further details about the film’s characters and story are still under wraps, but it will reportedly take place in the world of modern dating. Jonathan Schey is directing the comedy thriller movie from a screenplay he also wrote. Besides Egerton, the cast also includes Jessica Henwick (Glass Onion), Mia McKenna-Bruce (The Beatles), Charly Clive, and Herbert Nordrum (The Worst Person in the World). Cecilia Frugiuele and Olivier Kaempfer are producing for Parkville Pictures. It hails from Studiocanal Film4, Parkville Pictures, and LuckyChap, with Studiocanal and Film4 fully financing the project. Ron Halpern, Joe Naftalin, and Isobel Carter are overseeing the movie on behalf of Studiocanal, while Farhana Bhula and David Kimbangi will oversee for Film4. Egerton’s most recent acting credit was the Apple TV crime miniseries Smoke. Besides Everybody Wants to F— Me, he is also currently attached to star opposite Charlize Theron in Netflix’s upcoming action thriller Apex. Brooks On ‘Ella McCay’ Origins, Meeting Albert Brooks & ‘I’ll Do Anything’ War Stories – Crew Call Podcast View All November 19, 2025 5:21pm Glen Powell Getty Images The A24 thriller Huntington starring Glen Powell, Ed Harris and Margaret Qualley is getting re-titled as How to Make a Killing. In addition, we’ve confirmed that the movie is hitting theaters on Feb. 20 versus 20th Century Studios’ horror movie Psycho Killer and Lionsgate’s faith-based title I Can Only Imagine 2. Deadline first told you about the John Patton Ford project which is inspired by Studiocanal’s 1949 Ealing Comedy library title Kind Hearts and Coronets , starring Alec Guinness. Studiocanal financed the latest iteration and also produced. Jessica Henwick, Zach Woods, Topher Grace and Bill Camp also star. Kind Hearts And Coronets follows Louis D’Ascoyne Mazzini, the son of a woman disowned by her aristocratic family for marrying out of her social class. After her death, a vengeful Louis decides to take the family’s dukedom by murdering the eight people ahead of him in the line of succession to the title. The BAFTA-nominated film was included in Time ‘s 2005 list of the top 100 films since 1923. Ford’s screenplay was ranked on the 2014 Black List then titled Rothchild. At one point, Shia LaBeouf and Mel Gibson were set to star under the direction of Jon S. Baird. Powell currently has Paramount’s The Running Man in theaters. Through Tuesday, the movie stands at $19.4M at the domestic box office. The actor currently stars and executive produces the Hulu series Chad Powers. A24 has the feature films Eternity releasing on Nov. 26 with Miles Teller, Elizabeth Olsen, Callum Turner and Da’Vine Joy Randolph, as well as the Josh Safdie directed Marty Supreme starring Timothée Chalamet and Gwyneth Paltrow. How to Make a Killing is set to release on February 20, 2026. “The film follows Becket Redfellow (Powell), heir to a multibillion-dollar fortune, who will stop at nothing to get what he deserves … or what he thinks he deserves,” a description of the movie reads. Check out the first How to Make a Killing trailer below ( watch other trailers ): Who is in the How to Make a Killing trailer? Alongside Powell, How to Make a Killing also stars Margaret Qualley, Ed Harris, Jessica Henwick, Zach Woods, Topher Grace, Raff Law, and Bill Camp. Loosely based on 1949’s Kind Hearts and Coronets by Robert Hamer, Huntington is written and directed by John Patton Ford , who previously made 2022’s Emily the Criminal with Aubrey Plaza. The film, which has been in development since 2024, recently went through a name change. Previously titled Huntington, How to Make a Killing’s new name was recently reported after trailers of the film began popping up. It’s unclear why the film’s old name was changed. Powell has seen a meteoric rise to superstardom following his appearance in 2022’s Top Gun: Maverick. After that role, Powell starred in 2023’s Anyone But You and Hit Man, and then starred in 2024’s Twisters. This year, he led Edgar Wright’s adaptation of The Running Man, and he is also set to star in the upcoming J.J. Abrams film Ghostwriter, which is also set for a 2026 release date.
